asOf.baseline: Code snapshots 2026-09-03 (main, alpha) and 2026-09-07 (dev); study dated 2026-08-11

items.s: News Export
items.w: Added a News export to the admin Data page, producing an .xls file of articles with 15 columns including author, tags, visibility and exhibitor.
items.y: Organisers needed to download news data in a structured format to share, analyse and archive it.
items.o: Admins can export all news articles from /admin/data as an .xls file, in the language selected on the Exports page.

items.s: Formbuilder rework
items.w: Reworked the registration form builder, checking every field type on the registration page.
items.o: Registration form field types were re-checked as part of the form builder rework.

items.s: (New UI) My Basket for the participant
items.w: Built a participant basket in the new UI holding booked tickets, sessions and on-demand sessions, with sections, discount codes and per-section payment.
items.y: Participants need one place to collect booked tickets and sessions and pay now or later.
items.o: A basket popup opens whenever an item is added, showing subtotal, discount, tax and grand total, with Pay, Pay later and pay-per-section options.

items.s: (New Analytics UI) Meetings
items.w: Built the Meetings tab of the new global analytics module, with event, segment and date-range filters and web and app meeting metrics.
items.o: Organisers see requested meetings by status, online and offline counts, average meeting length, time in online meetings and request sources.

items.s: Product Brands export rework
items.w: Reworked the Product Brands export to run through SQS.
items.y: To make the Product Brands export quicker and more stable.
items.o: Admins download the Product Brands report via a queued export that contains all the respective information.

items.s: Meetings export rework
items.w: Reworked the Meetings export to run through SQS.
items.y: To make the Meetings export quicker and more stable.
items.o: Admins download the Meetings report via a queued export that contains all the respective information.

items.s: Exhibitor Daily Interactions export rework
Exhibitor Manual export rework
items.w: Reworked the Exhibitor Manual export to run through SQS.
items.y: The export needed to be quicker and more stable.
items.o: Admins download the Exhibitor Manual report via a queued job, with all respective information present in the file.

items.s: Automated provisioning for SAML
Messages export rework
items.w: Reworked the Messages export to run through SQS.
items.y: The Messages export needed to be quicker and more stable.
items.o: The Messages report is generated via an SQS queue and the downloaded file contains all the respective message data.

items.s: Seated Meetings export rework
items.w: Reworked the Seated Meetings export to run through SQS.
items.y: To make the Seated Meetings export quicker and more stable.
items.o: Seated Meetings reports are generated via an SQS-backed export and download with all respective information.

items.s: Android Sessions redesign
items.w: Redesigned session cards and session pages in the Android app to the updated design, with a pulsing Live tag, prices and a book button for paid sessions.
items.y: Session design needed aligning across web and mobile.
items.o: Android session lists, free and paid session pages match the new design, including live indication and paid session booking.

items.s: Create universal exceptions for API
Create ExceptionHandler for all APIs
IOS - Mobile App Components
Android - Mobile App Components
Backend API v2 with no restrictions
External Barcode and QR code
Change in Team Member Approval Process for Hosted Buyer Using Clients
items.w: Added a setting for private events with public registration so buyer-category team members need only a single Hosted Buyer acceptance.
items.y: Team members assigned a buyer category needed double approval, and each approval sent its own email.
items.o: When on, registered team members move straight to the buyer side with the Exhibitor buyer category, and only the buyer Accept email is sent.

items.s: Statistics: Remove deprecated methods from ExpoStatDB and replace to Statistics library
Statistics: Transfer to Statistics library all remaining methods from ExpoStatDB and replace them in the project
Statistics: Create ObjectType for Media (exhibitor, product)
Take out common parts from entry points
Create FieraMilano service
Full refactor of filters
items.w: Refactored the frontend filters so queries live in the components that use them, not in the filters component.
items.y: The previous filter logic caused conflicts and duplicated queries.
items.o: Filter queries run directly in their components, removing duplication and conflicts.

items.s: Total design re-check
items.w: Re-checked the design of profiles and profile editing, meetings, groups and RFP pages.
items.o: Profile, meeting, group and RFP screens were reviewed against the design.

items.s: Rewrite components to TypeScript
items.w: Rewrote platform frontend components in TypeScript as they were updated.
items.y: To control data types and reduce conflicts during development.
items.o: Updated components are typed in TypeScript.

items.s: Write unit tests to all new components
items.w: Added unit tests for all new frontend components, with the floor plan as a priority.
items.o: New components, including the floor plan, are covered by unit tests.

items.s: Upgrade Material to Mui5
items.w: Moved the frontend from the old Material UI library to MUI 5.
items.y: Two UI libraries were loaded and the old one was still used for most screens.
items.o: The frontend uses MUI 5 instead of two parallel UI libraries.

items.s: Check query type and do not change type when equal
items.w: Added a check that only reloads page data when query parameters have actually changed.
items.y: Pages reloaded their data on every load because query changes weren't detected.
items.o: Pages skip reloading when their query parameters are unchanged.

items.s: Refactoring meetings statuses
items.w: Refactored meeting statuses in the new and old frontends.
items.o: Meeting status handling was reworked across both frontends.

items.s: Rename in exhibitors table deprecated fields
items.w: Marked old hall, stand, image and video fields in the exhibitors table as deprecated and removed their code usages.
items.y: The data had moved to the stands relation and exhibitor events.
items.o: Exhibitors no longer use the deprecated fields; code reads stands and exhibitor events instead.

items.s: Create convenient RoleService
Delete sub_id field from table exhibitor_categories and ExhibitorCategories model
items.w: Removed the unused sub_id field from exhibitor categories and every place in the code that referenced it.
items.o: Exhibitor categories no longer carry the sub_id field.

items.s: Сache improvements (delete, multiple get)
items.w: Sent cache delete requests to the master host and investigated combining model and multi-key caching.
items.y: Cache deletes were being handled by a replica host.
items.o: Cache deletions go to the master host.

items.s: apidoc.php || generating of documentation
items.w: Extended the API documentation generator so responses can describe and link the object types they return.
items.y: To document which object types an API response can contain.
items.o: Generated API docs can reference response object types.

items.s: Add PDF-files validation and delete invalid PDF-files
items.w: Added validation that uploaded marketing content PDFs are not broken, and bulk-removed broken PDFs across the platform.
items.y: Broken PDFs caused thumbnail errors when marketing content was loaded.
items.o: Invalid PDFs are rejected on upload and existing broken files were cleaned up.

items.s: Change Code to scan QR codes for colocated events
items.w: Allowed mobile app users to scan badges of accounts from co-located events in the same database, behind a new contact-sharing toggle.
items.y: Users at co-located events needed to capture leads from badges belonging to other events on the same environment.
items.o: With the setting on, other-event scans are saved with an 'other event' ribbon, and scan reports and leads files gain an 'Event name' column.

items.s: Refactoring buildPermissionRelationsForbiddenQueries method
items.w: Replaced the model method that built forbidden permission-relation queries with the PermissionRelationsService.
items.o: Permission relation checks go through a single service.

items.s: Need ability to scan QR & Barcodes in the App that are not related to Expoplatform data without breaking the App.
items.w: Added an 'Allow users to scan any codes' setting so the mobile app can scan and store QR/barcodes unrelated to platform accounts.
items.y: Scanning a code not linked to platform data showed a 'not found' error instead of saving the scan.
items.o: With the setting on, unknown codes are saved as 'Code successfully scanned' and appear in a new 'Scanned code' column in lead and scan exports.

items.s: ExpoPlatform's Check-In app: Ability to scan external QR and Barcodes and capture the unique code number in reports
items.w: Let the check-in app scan external QR codes, barcodes and co-located event badges, and added scanned code and event name columns to the Check-in list report.
items.y: Organisers needed to scan any code or badge, including accounts attached to other events on the same environment.
items.o: Unknown codes are saved and listed rather than rejected, and the check-in report shows each scanned code and, if recognised, its event.

items.s: Mobile analytics MVP: Get the total logins and the total unique logged in users per app
items.w: Added a 'Mobile app logins' custom report in Analytics/Export: an XLS with iOS and Android tabs listing each user login with profile fields.
items.y: Organisers only saw app downloads and had no visibility of how their app was actually used.
items.o: Organisers can export logins per app, with ID, timestamp, name, email, company, job title and category, and derive total and unique logged-in users.

items.s: Front-end investigation and research
Create unit-test to check presence of all DI services
Table meeting setup and meeting cards improvements in app
items.w: Adapted the app to the new meeting wizard and table meetings: confirmed admin-created meetings, a meeting-type choice, zone and table selection.
items.y: The app had to match new admin-side meeting functionality.
items.o: In the app, admin-created meetings show as confirmed and marked as organiser-created, and table meetings are booked by zone, timeslot and table.

items.s: *FIME* Visitor QR redirect to 403 error
items.w: Moved the sign-in page settings to the new frontend landing page so scanned visitor QR codes no longer hit a 403 first.
items.y: Visitors scanning QR codes onsite saw a 403 error for a few seconds before the site loaded.
items.o: QR scans land on a configurable sign-in landing page without the 403 flash.

items.s: Improve AbstractCollection (& Map) functionality
Move discord notifications to a separate service from Utils
Mobile app for Floor Plan (web view only)
items.w: Replaced the old floor plan webview in the Android and iOS apps with the new front-end floor plan widget link.
items.o: The mobile apps open the new /newfront/widgets/floorplan webview, first visible in the test app.

items.s: Optimize writing data to dynamo becaouse of trothle
Create DTO and Map for Register form fields
Refactor statistics gathering on frontend new UI
EMEA: Ability for Company profile to add Custom questions for its team members in the Lead capture form, via a pool of Questions
items.w: Added a Lead Questions tab for exhibitor admins to create custom lead capture questions (text, select, radio and more) for their team members.
items.y: Team members could only answer the fixed default lead questions, and exhibitors wanted their own.
items.o: When enabled, exhibitor team members see their company's custom questions on the lead capture screen, with answers in the leads report.

items.s: Messenger mobile view (web)
items.w: Reworked the mobile web private chat page: back-to-list button, pinned header and input, hidden footer, and send-button-only messaging on mobile.
items.o: On mobile the chat has a fixed header and input with Enter adding a new line; the desktop hint now reads 'Press Enter to send'.

items.s: EMEA: Sponsored Session Should be Visible on Company Profile
items.w: Added a Sponsored Sessions block to the exhibitor profile in the webview, reusing the session card, slider and Show All behaviour.
items.y: A client required sessions an exhibitor sponsors to be visible on that exhibitor's profile, not only on the session page.
items.o: Exhibitor profiles automatically show a sponsored-sessions block when the exhibitor sponsors sessions, and hide it when they sponsor none.

items.s: Change app icons
items.w: Unified the style and size of icons across the application.
items.y: Icons throughout the application were inconsistent in style and size.
items.o: Application icons follow one consistent design style and size.

items.s: NA: Marketing content description to be extended to 3000 characters
items.w: Added a per-exhibitor-category 'File description characters limit' setting for marketing content and relaid the content screens with a More button.
items.y: A client wanted marketing content descriptions raised from 200 to 3,000 characters.
items.o: Organisers set the description limit per category (0 = unlimited, default 200); descriptions sit below the thumbnail and expand via a More button.

items.s: Product Description and Product Image Mandatory
items.w: Added 'Required product image' and 'Required product description' toggles to product form settings.
items.y: BeautyIstanbul wanted to make product image and description mandatory for exhibitors.
items.o: When on, exhibitors cannot save a product without a main picture or description, and the fields are marked with an asterisk.

items.s: Rewrite Phone field validation and country code substitution
items.w: Rewrote phone field validation and country code substitution.
items.y: The field duplicated country codes, showed the wrong default flag and applied wrong masks for some countries.
items.o: Phone numbers validate per country with the correct code and flag.

items.s: Multi-Language Email templates - Marketing
items.w: Added a language selector to Marketing Email Sender and Campaign template creation and editing, so templates can be set per language.
items.y: Multi-language templates existed for registration and system emails but were missing for marketing emails.
items.o: Marketing emails go out in each recipient's pre-selected language, with the default language used for recipients who have none.

items.s: New system field of "Language Preference" in the Registration Form.
items.w: Added a 'Language Preference' system field to the exhibitor and visitor registration forms, plus import and export support.
items.o: Registrants pick a language at sign-up (defaulting to the event language), and all their emails and system notifications use it.

items.s: Comments and Likes functionality v.1.1 (Live comments and Replies) || Feed & Groups
items.w: Added live mode and replies to comments in Feed & Groups.
items.o: Comments update live and users can reply to comments.

items.s: EMEA: Add the option to make custom text field as a website field
items.w: Added a 'website' option to custom text fields in exhibitor and visitor registration settings and made website fields clickable on the front.
items.y: Website values entered in custom fields were not clickable on the front end.
items.o: Custom text fields can be set as website fields, and those values render as clickable links on the front.

items.s: EMEA: Export QR Codes in pdf format - Participants & Exhibitor Companies
items.w: Added 'Export QR codes' to Management Participants and Exhibitors, generating a PDF of QR codes filtered by category and status, one per page with identifying details.
items.y: Organisers needed a bulk export of QR codes for filtered lists of companies, products and individuals, similar to badge export.
items.o: Organisers generate a background PDF with one 12 cm QR code per page and the holder's details, including external codes.

items.s: Cancel button for exports
items.w: Added a cancel button so organisers can stop any export manually.
items.o: Organisers can cancel a running export.

items.s: Add process percentage indication for exports
2-way sync with Reach5 for user creation and password update from EP
Settings to show/hide elements in Scan lists in app
Main menu of the Website builder
items.w: Built the Website builder main menu: add block, page switcher, device previews, language switcher, gallery, history, global settings, save and publish.
items.o: The Website builder has a main menu under the header giving access to blocks, pages, previews, global styles, version history and publishing.

items.s: Main menu - Add block
EMEA: Lead capture page - company name & person name clickable to lead the person to company profile/personal profile
items.w: Made the person's name and, for team members, the company name clickable on the mobile lead capture screen after a badge scan.
items.y: App users wanted to go straight from a scanned badge to the person's or company's profile.
items.o: Tapping the name opens the person's public profile; tapping a team member's company opens their exhibitor's profile; non-team members' company stays plain text.

items.s: Main menu - Gallery button
items.w: Built the Website Builder Gallery: upload images, videos and files, create nested folders, sort, switch gallery/list layouts, paginate, and manage files.
items.o: Organisers store and organise site media, with video conversion, file details, and rename, preview, move, copy, copy URL, download and delete actions.

items.s: Main parts 1-3
items.w: Introduced Exhibitor Events: exhibitors create events from the frontend, organisers approve or reject them, with limits set in Module Management.
items.o: Approved exhibitor events appear alongside regular sessions, share their tracks, types and settings, and can be filtered on the Sessions page.

items.s: Additional part - 4
items.w: Added exhibitor event settings: track and type visibility by category or role, child-exhibitor sharing, contact persons, invite links and a maximum event duration.
items.o: Exhibitors can create events at any time, attach team members as contacts and share invite links, within admin-set visibility and duration limits.

items.s: Main menu - Global settings
items.w: Built the Website Builder Global Settings screen with text styles, colours, buttons, favicon and SEO settings, including custom font upload.
items.o: Organisers set site-wide fonts (including CDN or uploaded TTF/OTF/WOFF fonts) and theme, text, status and other colours with live previews, then save or close.

items.s: Lead file changes for scans without lead capture
Additional participants in meetings for apps
EMEA: Add option for state/region and city field in the custom select field
items.w: Added State/Region and City as types for the custom Select form element in exhibitor and visitor registration settings.
items.o: Organisers can build custom select fields that list states/regions or cities.

items.s: API endpoints int the public API to pull out meeting data in its entirety
items.w: Added a paginated public API endpoint returning full meeting data, matching the fields of the meetings export file.
items.y: Clients needed to pull the meeting listing into an external system.
items.o: External systems can retrieve every meeting export field, from Meeting ID to Creator, through the API with pagination.

items.s: (New Analytics) Dashboard fixes
items.w: Fixed the new analytics dashboard widgets so each counts participants, exhibitors, content and actions to a defined rule based on the end date.
items.o: Dashboard widgets show totals present on the end date, plus live online participants by top countries and top interest and activity categories.

items.s: (New Analytics) Registration fixes
items.w: Defined the registration widgets for the new analytics: exhibitor, participant and team member registrations over time, by category, country, interests and activities.
items.o: New analytics shows registration counts over time and breakdowns by category, country and top interest/activity categories for each audience type.

items.s: (New Analytics) Marketplace fixes
(New Analytics) Content fixes
items.w: Defined the content widgets for the new analytics: counts and average daily views, adds or downloads with period change, trending topics and leaderboards.
items.o: New analytics shows performance for news, sessions, on-demand, webinars and downloads, with top-content leaderboards.

items.s: Deleagate page subtabs for all user roles
Fields rotation for 180 degrees in Badge builder
items.w: Added a 180-degree rotation setting for each field, including QR codes, in the physical badge builder.
items.o: Rotated fields show in the badge preview and print rotated wherever the badge is printed.

items.s: Fields aligning in Badge builder
items.w: Added an alignment setting (Centred, Left, Right) for every field in the physical badge builder.
items.o: Each badge field can be aligned centre, left or right, reflected in the preview and wherever the badge is printed.

items.s: Fields duplication in Badge builder
items.w: Added field duplication to the physical badge builder and merged the Bar/QR/Both/Without fields into a single cloneable Code field.
items.y: Organisers needed the same badge data shown more than once with different display settings.
items.o: Badge fields, including codes, can be cloned many times with separate display settings, toggled individually and removed.

items.s: Category field movable on Badge builder
items.w: Made the Category field movable in the physical badge builder, like the other badge fields.
items.y: The Category field was static while all other fields could be repositioned.
items.o: Organisers drag the Category field to any position on the badge.

items.s: Fields Margin Left and Right in Badge builder
items.w: Added Left Margin and Right Margin settings to every field in the physical Badge builder, including QR codes.
items.o: Badge field margins set in the builder show in the preview and apply wherever the badge is printed.

items.s: QR code and Barcode resize in Badge builder
items.w: Added a percentage size setting (default 100%) for QR codes and barcodes in the physical Badge builder.
items.o: Resized QR codes and barcodes show in the badge preview and print at that size everywhere.

items.s: Custom Meeting Wizard Report rework
items.w: Reworked the Custom Meeting Wizard Report export to run through SQS.
items.y: The export needed to be quicker and more stable.
items.o: Admins download the Custom Meeting Wizard Report via a queued job, with all respective information present in the file.

items.s: (APP) Meeting request includes the attached file option
items.w: Added an optional file attachment to the regular meeting request flow in the app, enabled by a new toggle in meeting settings.
items.o: When enabled, requesters can attach a file to a meeting request, and recipients can open or download it from the meeting card in their schedule.

items.s: Print badge statistics capture
items.w: Captured badge printing statistics wherever badges are printed: admin panel, frontend, kiosk and emails.
items.o: Badge prints are recorded across every printing channel.

items.s: Floorplan Admin Panel - add Exhibitor name & Stand label + Hide Stand mode
items.w: Showed exhibitor names and stand labels on floor plan stands, scaled by zoom, with parent-exhibitor logic and options to hide stands and stand labels.
items.y: Visitors had to search the floor plan by stand name, which was confusing; the search needed to work by exhibitor name.
items.o: Floor plan stands show the exhibitor name above the stand number on web and app, and admins can hide individual stands or stand labels per hall.

items.s: Floorplan Admin Panel - Ability to Draw/Delete Stands
Images download rework in applications
items.w: Replaced app image requests to the server with static image links carried in synced objects.
items.o: The apps load exhibitor, session and account images from static links.

items.s: Allow selection of number of characters for the news description
items.w: Added an 'Article characters limit' setting per exhibitor category, replacing the hardcoded 1,000-character cap on exhibitor news.
items.y: The client wanted exhibitors to publish full news articles, with limits configurable from 1,000 to 10,000 characters.
items.o: Organisers set the news character limit per category (0 for unlimited); existing over-limit articles stay but cannot be saved until trimmed.

items.s: Refactoring of AbstractIndexQueryBuilder
items.w: Refactored the search index query builder towards a fluent interface for equals, contains, starts/ends-with and fuzzy matching.
items.o: Index queries are built through a composable builder.

items.s: Forbid exhibitors to add active products for those who are not allowed & let them arrive on Active products by default in the company profile.
items.w: Added settings to block product creation once an exhibitor's active-product limit is reached and to choose the default products tab.
items.y: Exhibitors added products that stayed inactive without noticing, then complained after learning active products were a paid option.
items.o: Organisers can disable '+ Add Product' at the limit, set All/Active/Inactive as the default tab; a disclaimer and toggle tooltips explain status.

items.s: Adding More Variables in Visitor Confirmation Page
items.w: Added a 'Print Your Badge' variable for the visitor registration confirmation page.
items.y: BeautyIstanbul users often missed emails due to unverified domains and Turkish İ/ı typos, so could not get their badges.
items.o: The confirmation page shows a Print Badge link that opens the user's badge in a new tab, the same as the admin and profile print option.

items.s: Create one component which will control all available integrations for project
items.w: Created one component to control all integrations available for a project.
items.o: Integrations are managed from a single component.

items.s: Web secure fixes
items.w: Fixed security issues in the frontend, admin panel and server listed in a security report supplied by a client.
items.y: A client's security report flagged vulnerabilities in the platform.
items.o: The reported security issues across frontend, admin panel and server were addressed.

items.s: Applications secure fixes
items.w: Fixed security issues in the Android and iOS apps listed in a security report supplied by a client.
items.y: A client's security report flagged vulnerabilities in the mobile apps.
items.o: The reported security issues in the Android and iOS apps were addressed.

items.s: Filter and pagination retention after booking meetings
items.w: Added a meeting setting to return users to the page where they started a meeting request, keeping filters and pagination.
items.y: Vinexposium buyers lost their many marketplace filters after requesting a meeting, which was possible to avoid in the old UI.
items.o: Organisers choose between the meetings page and the initiating page; from marketplace and delegate lists users return with filters and page retained.

items.s: Allow displayment of Speakers with INACTIVE status on the frontend
items.w: Added a Show inactive speakers on the frontend toggle to registration settings, covering inactive, invited, uploaded and approved speaker statuses.
items.y: Inactive speakers were hidden on the web, so visitors could not see the full speaker list or network with them.
items.o: When the toggle is on, speakers without an active account appear in frontend speaker lists; blocked, banned and waitlisted speakers stay hidden.

items.s: We need add Visit Connect URL in the GES Integration while mapping Team members
Auto confirmation of meetings | Participant Category Level
items.w: Added a 'Meeting autoconfirm' toggle at participant-category level, extending the existing event-wide auto-confirmation setting.
items.y: Organisers wanted meeting auto-confirmation for specific participant categories rather than the whole event.
items.o: Meeting requests sent by participants in an enabled category confirm automatically and the Pending status is hidden once no pending meetings remain.

items.s: Refactoring api for app with appointsments.
items.w: Refactored the app API for cancelling and confirming appointments to use the Schedule service, removing an unused check action.
items.o: App appointment actions share the Schedule service.

items.s: Optimization in ScheduleService -> checkTimes function
items.w: Optimised the schedule time check so the time service is initialised once instead of twice.
items.y: The schedule time arrays were being loaded twice per check.
items.o: Meeting time checks do less repeated work.

items.s: Edit refresh logic in all checkQueueExportStatus
items.w: Fixed the refresh flag in export status checks so polling continues until the file URL is ready.
items.o: Export status endpoints report refresh correctly until the download is ready.

items.s: Passwordless logination
items.w: Added passwordless one-time-password login on the front end, plus an admin-panel OTP button and an event setting to switch it on.
items.y: Admins needed a way to help users with login trouble straight away by giving them a one-time password.
items.o: Users log in with an emailed OTP valid for 3 minutes, with a 15-second resend cooldown; admins can generate and copy an OTP for any exhibitor or visitor.

items.s: Add Badges Variable in "Visitor Switch Category" Template
items.w: Added badge variables (print badge link, badge barcode, badge QR code, print badge QR code) to the 'Visitor Switch to Category' registration email template.
items.y: The template had no badge variables, which a client needed.
items.o: Visitors who switch category can receive their badge print link and codes in that email.

items.s: EMEA. Custom Questions stage2. Additional questions
items.w: Extended lead capture additional questions with select, multiselect, radio group, checkbox and checkbox group types.
items.y: The first stage supported only simple text inputs for additional questions.
items.o: Organisers add custom lead questions of six types through a pop-up, with configurable answer options, on the admin and front end.

items.s: Sponsor banners in profile
items.w: Added one- or two-banner sponsor slots to every page of Exhibitor and Visitor My profile, configured per sponsor and in sponsor settings.
items.o: Sponsors can be assigned banners on My profile pages per device; banners rotate between sponsors and link out, with an external-link warning if enabled.

items.s: Include session interactions in the  dashboard of exhibitor who is sponsoring it
items.w: Added 'Booked a session' and 'Attended session' columns to the sponsoring exhibitor's dashboard interactions table.
items.y: Exhibitor-sponsors wanted to see everyone who booked or attended the sessions they sponsor.
items.o: Sponsors see who booked or attended (online, offline or on demand) their sponsored sessions, and the data remains after sponsorship ends.

items.s: Meeting request swager documentation
items.w: Wrote Swagger documentation with test data for meeting requests.
items.o: Meeting request endpoints are documented in Swagger.

items.s: Integration with ASP events system to pull in Exhibitors, Sessions and Speakers
items.w: Built an integration with the ASP events API to pull exhibitors, sessions and speakers, with a configurable site UUID per event.
items.y: Four ASP-run shows needed exhibitor, session and speaker data imported from ASP into ExpoPlatform.
items.o: Exhibitors (linked by account number, updated by modified date), speakers and sessions sync from ASP; main contacts become admin team members.

items.s: Need possibility to display 24 items on the catalogue page instead of 12 by default
items.w: Added a general setting for the default number of marketplace items per page (8 to 60, default 12).
items.y: The organiser sells top catalogue spots to exhibitors, so showing 24 instead of 12 doubles that revenue.
items.o: The marketplace opens with the per-page count set in admin; existing events keep 12.

items.s: Need Possibility to add the 'notes' present in exhibitor profile in BO in Excel export file
items.w: Added a 'Notes' column and export checkbox to the Exhibitors export, carrying the Notes field from the exhibitor profile in the admin panel.
items.y: Organisers record call notes on exhibitor profiles but could not see them in the export, making follow-up hard.
items.o: The Exhibitors export includes each exhibitor's notes when 'All fields' or the 'Notes' checkbox is selected.

items.s: Code improvement
items.w: Rewrote the meeting setup component to use a reducer.
items.o: Meeting setup state is managed with useReducer.

items.s: lead questions: remove copy-paste blocks
items.w: Removed duplicated copy-paste blocks from the lead questions script.
items.o: The lead questions script has no duplicated blocks.

items.s: Create root enums for not-root enums
items.w: Created root-level enums for enums that lived outside the shared Enums folder.
items.o: Enums are centralised, ready to be split into domain folders later.

items.s: Android/ Update search list behaviour

items.s: Client Manager: Organizer can send Event emails with a default no-reply reply address

items.s: Organizer Onboarding Journey
items.w: A guided onboarding flow takes new organisers through account, event and billing setup and recommends modules suited to their event.
items.y: Part of the Onboarding Journey: reduce setup friction and drive activation and module adoption after signup.

items.s: Onboarding Dashboard
items.w: An event onboarding dashboard gives TAMs and organisers one place to see setup progress per module, manage team members and resume onboarding.

items.s: Round Tables. Remove Deleted Users from Sessions

items.s: IMEX Requirements (Application)
items.w: Attendees get a rebuilt search experience with grouped typeahead, a Top Results block, quick links and no dead-end pages, per IMEX requirements.
items.y: IMEX requirement for search; application layer on top of the Qdrant ranking rebuild.
items.o: Grouped typeahead with Quick Link chips, a results page with Top Results, quick links and fixed organiser-ordered entity blocks with Show more, and no-dead-end states.

items.s: Prioritizing name matches over description matches
items.w: Reworked AI exhibitor search so exact partner name matches outrank coordinators that merely mention the term in their description, ensuring buyers at IMEX land on the right company.
items.y: Hive Requirement - a confirmed relevance blocker surfaced during the IMEX Qdrant search pilot.
items.o: Introduced hybrid name-priority scoring on top of semantic search so name-field matches always score above description-level hits across exhibitor entities.

items.s: Prototype for IMEX demo
items.w: Built a lightweight branded search front-end so the AI search pilot could be demonstrated to IMEX stakeholders without raw API calls.
items.y: Hive Requirement - needed to evaluate and showcase the IMEX search pilot to stakeholders.
items.o: Delivered a polished demo UI with a search box and typeahead autocomplete that calls the search and /autocomplete endpoints and groups results by entity type.

items.s: Overlenient substring matching pulling in noise
items.w: Routed partial-name typeahead through a dedicated fast autocomplete endpoint so over-lenient substring matching no longer floods AI search with noise.
items.y: Hive Requirement - search-noise blocker identified in the IMEX Qdrant pilot.
items.o: Added a separate prefix-indexed /autocomplete endpoint (~50ms) that keeps noisy substring behaviour out of full search and surfaces clean name suggestions.

items.s: Spaces and special characters breaking name matches
items.w: Made AI search resilient to spacing and special-character differences so a query like 'Visit Scotland' still finds 'VisitScotland'.
items.y: Hive Requirement - confirmed name-matching blocker for the IMEX pilot.
items.o: Tokeniser handling was fixed so spaced and unspaced/concatenated brand-name variants resolve to the correct exhibitor in top results.

items.s: No alias or multi-lingual variant handling
items.w: Added cultural-name and diacritic tolerance to AI search so endonym/exonym variants (e.g. 'Italia' for 'Italy') return the right exhibitors.
items.y: Hive Requirement - multilingual matching gap raised in the IMEX pilot.
items.o: Combined semantic similarity with ascii_folding character normalisation so common language variants and diacritic differences surface relevant results instead of zero results.

items.s: Coordinator/partner ranking hierarchy
items.w: Encoded the coordinator/partner hierarchy into AI search so exhibitor results follow a consistent parent/child ranking order.
items.y: Hive Requirement - hierarchy ranking requirement from the IMEX pilot.
items.o: Extracted the parent/child relationship from PostgreSQL into the Qdrant payload during ingestion, enabling coordinator-exact, partner-exact, coordinator-fuzzy, partner-fuzzy ordering.

items.s: People, Session, Products, News entity not indexed
items.w: Extended AI search coverage by indexing People, Sessions, Products and News so name matches across all entity types rank correctly.
items.y: Hive Requirement - entity-coverage gap identified in the IMEX pilot.
items.o: Indexed the People, News, Product and Session entities in Qdrant so exact name matches surface and rank above weaker description-level matches, consistent with other entity types.

items.s: Weak recovery states/dead ends
items.w: Replaced empty AI-search dead-ends with helpful 'Did you mean...?' and category fallback prompts so buyers always have a next step.
items.y: Hive Requirement - poor recovery-state experience flagged in the IMEX pilot.
items.o: Added fallback handling so a no-results query surfaces a no-results message with 'Did you mean...?' suggestions and category prompts rather than an empty page.

items.s: Change meeting rating trigger in app
items.w: Meeting ratings now surface in the mobile app as soon as attendees receive their final schedule, capturing feedback earlier in the meeting-program lifecycle.
items.y: Customer Request / Operational Efficiency - timing the ratings trigger to the Final Schedule lets organizers collect richer, more timely meeting feedback.
items.o: Ratings become available for each meeting at the moment it appears in the app via the Final Schedule, rather than only after the program concludes.

items.s: Fix EP-32657 and apply changes to NEXT12
items.w: Backported the EP-32657 fix to NEXT12 to keep that version consistent with other platform versions.
items.y: Keeps NEXT12 in sync with fixes delivered to other versions.
items.o: The EP-32657 fix was applied to NEXT12.

items.s: Calendar View (Events) - Admin Panel
items.w: Redesigns the Admin Panel events calendar with year-to-day time-scale views, search, filtering and click-through to each event's detail page.
items.y: Part of the broader Admin Panel redesign, bringing the calendar in line with the updated experience.
items.o: Specified: a calendar that toggles Year, 6-month, 3-month, Month, Week and Day views, with event search, filters and navigation to the event detail page.

items.s: Aanlytics View - Admin Panel
items.w: Visually redesigns the Admin Panel Customers/analytics screen to match the new admin style while keeping all existing columns, filters and statistics.
items.y: Part of the Admin Panel redesign; consistency of typography, colours, spacing and components across the panel.
items.o: Specified as a visual-only redesign following the design handoff, preserving region selector, event table, statistics columns, date and dropdown filters, 365 badge and pagination.

items.s: [admin-ui] Rewrite files inside /plugins to TS
items.w: Rewrote files inside the admin panel's /plugins folder to TypeScript as part of the ongoing JS-to-TS migration.
items.y: Part of an ongoing effort to migrate the admin UI to TypeScript for better maintainability.
items.o: Files inside /plugins rewritten in TypeScript.

items.w: Rewrote files inside the admin panel's /utils folder to TypeScript as part of the ongoing JS-to-TS migration.
items.y: Part of an ongoing effort to migrate the admin UI to TypeScript for better maintainability.
items.o: Files inside /utils rewritten in TypeScript.

items.y: Part of an ongoing effort to migrate the admin UI to TypeScript for better maintainability.
items.o: Files inside /hooks rewritten in TypeScript.

items.s: Add tests for helpers and common components
items.w: Adds automated tests for frontend helpers and common components (ticket has no further detail).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; the ticket is on hold.

items.s: Display AI Meeting Notetaker as an Add-on under Lead Capture Pro in the Exhibitor profile on the front-end allowing them to purchase it
items.w: Exhibitors can now buy AI Meeting Notes directly on the Lead Capture Pro page, instantly unlocking AI transcription for their whole team.
items.y: Completes the Lead Capture Pro monetisation flow so the AI add-on can convert to revenue; part of the AI-first paradigm.
items.o: The Lead Capture Pro purchasing page shows a buyable AI Meeting Notes option when enabled, flips to a Purchased state after checkout, and grants the exhibitor and all team members access on web and mobile via the aiNoteTakerEnabled flag.

items.s: Side Menu - Admin Panel
items.w: Introduces a new expandable/collapsible side menu as the primary Admin Panel navigation for TAMs, Finance and future roles.
items.y: Part of the Admin Panel redesign, giving every admin role one consistent way to reach top-level sections.
items.o: Specified: side menu with Customers Environments, Team Management, Settings and a user profile card, expanded and collapsed states, tooltips, active-page highlight and session-persistent state.

items.s: Client Manager Actions
items.w: Adds a three-dot action menu to each customer environment row so TAMs can reach details, keys, settings, API logs, edit and delete in one place.
items.y: Part of the Admin Panel redesign within the Onboarding Journey, reducing clicks for routine environment management.
items.o: Specified: an eight-item contextual menu (Customer Details, App Updates, Key, Unique Accounts, Settings, API Logs, Edit, Delete) with a confirmation step before deletion.

items.s: Two-party consent mechanism
items.w: Adds a two-party consent layer to AI Notes recordings: an environment acknowledgement for the initiator and tiered consent or notification for the recipient, with a full audit trail.
items.y: Compliance: IMEX GDPR requirements and German recording law (§201 StGB) require informed consent and per-recording awareness.
items.o: Specified: once-per-event initiator acknowledgement, Tier 1 full consent and Tier 2 lightweight notification for recipients, a persistent recording indicator and consent audit logging.

items.s: Data deletion access
items.w: Gives AI Notes recipients a way to have their recordings deleted and defines what server-side deletion and data retention must cover.
items.y: Compliance: GDPR Articles 17 and 5(1)(e), raised under the IMEX GDPR requirements.
items.o: Specified: a recipient deletion route (self-service or DSAR), removal of audio, transcript, summary, metadata and cached outputs, preserved consent audit logs, and a defined, disclosed retention policy.

items.s: Improve Sponsorship export generation
items.w: Made Sponsorship statistics export generation reliable for large datasets, fixing failures reported in EP-46119.
items.y: Reported failures needed a durable fix so exports reliably complete regardless of data volume.
items.o: Sponsorship export generation improved to reliably complete even with large amounts of data.

items.s: Random sorting for Sponsors and Sponsored products
items.w: Sponsors and sponsored products on the marketplace can be sorted by matchmaking, set priority, or a new random order on each refresh.
items.y: Clients with hundreds of sponsors were frustrated that users always saw the same top sponsors.
items.o: Organisers can rotate sponsor exposure fairly, on web and app.

items.s: Add Unit Test report to Sonar for adminUI
items.w: Wired adminUI's unit test reports into SonarQube so coverage, bugs and code issues are visible for that project.
items.y: Improves visibility into code quality to catch issues earlier.
items.o: adminUI unit test coverage now tracked in SonarQube.

items.s: Integration Hub – ensure account username is updated when email changes
items.w: Fixed Integration Hub to keep account username in sync with email changes, and added tests/docs so login/matching doesn't break.
items.y: Needed to prevent broken login/matching assumptions for integrated accounts, and to formalize the already-implemented behavior with docs and tests.
items.o: Username now updates in sync with email changes (when username was email-derived), conflicts are handled safely, and the behavior is documented and covered by tests.

items.s: Native integrations documentation
items.w: Three-tier documentation for Native Integrations on the new Abstract Integration Schema was produced, equipping developers, managers, and clients to operate post-migration integrations.
items.y: Internal Efficiency / Maintenance - documentation reduces support escalations and onboarding friction as integrations move to the new schema.
items.o: Developer, manager, and client-level documentation was created covering architecture and data flows, business capabilities, and client-facing configuration and troubleshooting.

items.s: Investigate getUserRole in src\utils\helpers\helpers.ts (after https://bitbucket.org/expoplatform/admin-ui/pull-requests/2872 will be merged)
items.w: Investigated whether getUserRole's handling of multi-role arrays was correct, following a reviewer's concern on a related PR.
items.y: Needed to verify whether the flagged concern about role-array ordering was a real bug.
items.o: Current getUserRole behavior investigated and clarified.

items.s: Centralised Management for Speed Networking, Meeting Program, and Concierge Meetings
items.w: A new Meeting Formats menu in the Admin Panel holding Speed Networking, Meeting Program and Concierge Meetings settings, with Concierge zones in their own tab.
items.y: So organisers manage every meeting format from one place instead of several admin areas.
items.o: Existing settings move unchanged into Meeting Formats, stay scoped to the event and follow existing permissions.

items.s: Email Templates Management for Speed Networking, Meeting Program, and Concierge Meetings in Admin Panel
items.w: Email templates tabs for Speed Networking, Meeting Program and Concierge Meetings inside Meeting Formats; Concierge's general templates stay in sync both ways.
items.y: So organisers manage each meeting format's emails in its own area instead of a generic Meetings email section.
items.o: Existing templates move with their triggers intact, and edits stay scoped to the event.

items.s: Email Templates Management for Exhibitor Events and Round Tables in Meeting Formats
items.w: Email templates tabs for Exhibitor Events and Round Tables inside Meeting Formats; shared templates warn before a save affects other places.
items.y: So organisers configure each format's emails without accidentally changing emails for other sessions.
items.o: Exhibitor Events' organiser and exhibitor notifications move to their format; shared templates show where else they're used.

items.s: Enhancements to Exhibitor Events Management in Meeting Formats for Organizers
items.w: Exhibitor Events get their own section in Meeting Formats: events list and create, speakers and moderators, config, and tags, tracks and types.
items.y: So organisers manage exhibitor events separately from general sessions without unintended side effects.
items.o: Exhibitor events are managed apart from sessions; edits to shared speakers, tags or settings show a 'used in other locations' warning.

items.s: Independent Management for Round Tables in Admin Panel
items.w: Round Tables get their own section in Meeting Formats: list and create, moderators, config, and tags, tracks and types, separate from sessions.
items.y: So organisers configure round tables without going through the sessions module or affecting other session types.
items.o: Round tables are managed on their own, with exhibitor-event-only columns hidden and warnings when shared data is edited.

items.s: AI note taker consent mechanism
items.w: Adds a consent mechanism to the AI note taker (ticket has no further detail).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; sits under moving the Meeting Transcription Tool from POC to production.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

items.s: AI note taker data deletion controls
items.w: Adds data deletion controls to the AI note taker (ticket has no further detail).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; sits under moving the Meeting Transcription Tool from POC to production.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

items.s: Admin Panel Scope Restriction
items.w: Lets organisers restrict AI Notes to all badge scans, scheduled meetings only or specific attendee types, enforced in the app and on the server.
items.y: Compliance and client request: IMEX preferred limiting AI Notes to scheduled meetings to reduce GDPR risk.
items.o: Specified: per-event scope settings for admins, the Record button hidden for non-qualifying scans and server-side rejection of non-qualifying uploads.

items.s: Lead Capture Access Control by Exhibitor Category
items.w: Lead Capture access moves from a global Exhibitor Manual setting to a per exhibitor-category toggle; buying Lead Capture Pro always grants access.
items.y: Organisers need to offer lead capture to some exhibitors only, free or as part of Lead Capture Pro.
items.o: Exhibitors and their teams get lead capture in the app only if their category allows it or they bought it.

items.s: Lead Capture: Exhibitor-Level Granular Control
items.w: A per-exhibitor Lead capture toggle that follows the exhibitor's category, with a custom override and reset; Lead Capture Pro buyers always get access.
items.y: Organisers need to grant lead capture to individual exhibitors, e.g. for free, not just by category.
items.o: Organisers switch lead capture on or off for one exhibitor and their team without affecting others in the category.

items.s: Product QR Codes: Category-Level Access Control
items.w: Product QR codes move from a global setting to a per exhibitor-category toggle, off by default; buying Lead Capture Pro always grants access.
items.y: Organisers need to give product QR codes to some exhibitors only, e.g. free for some or as part of Lead Capture Pro.
items.o: Exhibitors see product QR codes in product editing on web only when their category allows it or they bought it.

items.s: Product QR Codes: Exhibitor-Level Access Control
items.w: A per-exhibitor Product QR codes toggle that follows the exhibitor's category, with a custom override and reset; Lead Capture Pro still takes priority.
items.y: Organisers need to grant product QR codes to individual exhibitors, not only whole categories.
items.o: Organisers can switch product QR codes on or off for one exhibitor without affecting the rest of its category.

items.s: Lead Capture Pro — Settings Consolidation
items.w: Exhibitor category and profile settings gain Lead Capture, Product QR Codes and AI Meeting Notes, grouped with lead questions in one Lead Capture Pro block.
items.y: Only lead questions were available per exhibitor; the other Lead Capture Pro features needed the same control.
items.o: Organisers manage every Lead Capture Pro feature for categories and exhibitors from one consistent block.

items.s: Restructure Module Management for Meeting Format
items.w: Module Management gets a Meeting Formats group with a toggle each for Speed Networking, Meeting Program, Concierge Meetings, Exhibitor Events and Round Tables.
items.y: So the Meeting Formats menu reflects which formats are actually switched on for the event.
items.o: Organisers switch each meeting format on or off independently; existing events keep their current state.

items.s: Profile Picture sync in GES/Visit integration
items.w: Attendee profile pictures now sync back to the GES/Visit integration with EP as the source of truth, keeping partner systems visually consistent with the EP platform.
items.y: Customer Request / Internal Efficiency - a requested integration capability that keeps profile imagery consistent while avoiding update loops by making EP the source of truth.
items.o: A profile-picture push-back capability was implemented for the GES/Visit integration, with profile pictures excluded from update mappings to prevent infinite update loops.

items.s: Android app: migrate download screen to use workmanager
items.w: Migrated the Android download screen to WorkManager for more reliable background download handling, keeping all existing features.
items.y: Improves reliability of background downloads on Android.
items.o: Download screen now fully functional on WorkManager with all existing download features retained.

items.s: Revisit BM filtering for inference part of recommendation service
items.w: Business Matching filters in the new recommendation service were reviewed and test-covered, ensuring the matchmaking engine produces accurate recommendations.
items.y: Platform Health / Internal Efficiency - verifying BM filters protects the integrity of the matchmaking recommendations the platform relies on.
items.o: BM filter behaviour was reviewed and understood, automated tests were added for each filter, and issues were either fixed or captured as linked follow-up tasks.

items.s: Show notification bubble on mobile app
items.w: Shows numeric unread badges on the mobile app icon so attendees and exhibitors notice messages, meeting requests and schedule changes, with an opt-out setting.
items.y: Client request from Busworld 2027, which runs as an ongoing community on the mobile app.
items.o: Specified: real-time app-icon badge counters capped at 99+, a default-on settings toggle stored server-side, independent of push notifications.

items.s: Random sorting for sponsors in app
items.w: The mobile app now supports matchmaking-based and randomized sorting of sponsors and sponsored products, aligning mobile sponsor visibility with the new web admin controls.
items.y: Revenue Opportunity / Product Vision - matching mobile to the new sponsor-sorting settings ensures fair sponsor rotation and relevance on the most-used surface, protecting sponsorship value.
items.o: Mobile now reads the active sorting mode from the API and renders sponsors and sponsored products By matchmaking (score order) or Random (in-app shuffle, re-shuffled on each screen re-entry), while preserving existing set-priority behaviour and display limits.

items.s: Move require section to the server side (useRedirectByRequirements)
items.w: Moves the profile-requirements redirect to the server so users with incomplete profiles are redirected before the page renders, removing a visible flash.
items.y: Technical debt: the hook carried a TODO to move server-side, and the flash hurts user experience.
items.o: Specified: server-side redirects to /profile/edit or /profile/video, preserved on-page toast behaviour and removal of client router-based redirect logic.

items.s: Android/ Phone and E-mail sections missed under lead capture screen
items.w: Fixed the Android lead capture screen where Contact details (phone/email) were missing entirely instead of following the configured show/hide setting.
items.y: Flagged against the design requirement (Figma spec) that this field should be conditionally shown, not omitted.
items.o: Contact details field restored on the lead capture screen, respecting the show/hide setting.

items.s: Recommendation slider on community page look different from design
items.w: Fixed the community page's recommendation slider so its appearance matches the approved Figma design.
items.y: Visual inconsistency with the approved design needed correcting.
items.o: Recommendation slider now matches the design.

items.s: Name matches not prioritized in autocomplete suggestion results
items.w: Search autocomplete now prioritises name matches over description matches, so attendees see the most relevant entity at the top of suggestion results.
items.y: Customer Request / Product Vision - correct result ranking is essential to the AI search experience being piloted for events like IMEX.
items.o: Autocomplete ranking was changed so name matches are prioritised over description matches across and within entity types.

items.s: Hash check in integration update flow considers inactive AccountEvents
items.w: Fixes the integration update hash check so previously deactivated visitors and exhibitors are reactivated when their data is reprocessed.
items.y: Data integrity in integration imports: re-sent records must restore event participation.
items.o: Suggested fix: hash checks use active-only AccountEvents and skip comparison when none exists, letting the update proceed.

items.s: Website Builder: Organizer can hide the button on individual Cards
items.w: Website Builder now lets organizers hide the call-to-action button on individual cards via a per-card toggle, removing the previous reliance on custom CSS.
items.y: Self-Service / Customer Request - a per-card toggle removes a custom-CSS workaround and gives organizers direct, code-free control.
items.o: A per-card toggle was added to the Website Builder card component so organizers can show or hide the button on each card independently.

items.s: [CLONING] [BE] Cloning Refactor
items.w: Refactored the event cloning system from an 800-line god class into a handler-registry pipeline, adding logging, partial-failure resilience, and easy extensibility.
items.y: Technical debt in cloning was blocking the ability to safely add new cloneable entities and diagnose failures, and needed to be tackled before further extending cloning.
items.o: Cloning now uses a handler-registry + pipeline model: a new clone handler is a single new file with zero core changes, a single handler failure no longer halts the whole clone, every handler execution is logged with status/duration/error, clone logic was removed from the Events model, and the orchestrator shrank to ~50 lines.

items.s: Organizer toggle to enable feedback form and create report
items.w: Adds an organiser toggle to switch on mobile-app event feedback collection and a downloadable Event Feedback report of submissions.
items.y: Part of Attendance & Event Analytics 2026, giving organisers attendee feedback data.
items.o: Specified: an off-by-default Event Feedback toggle after OTP Authentication that flags the app, stored submissions, and a report with rating, text, timestamp, name, email and role.

items.s: Add border and shadow options for individual card views
items.w: Closed a styling-consistency gap in Website Builder so every static card view can carry borders and shadows, giving organizers a uniform, professional event-site look without design hacks.
items.y: Operational Efficiency and UX consistency - to remove design workarounds and align card behaviour across the builder, raising the quality of organizer-built event websites.
items.o: Border and shadow options were added to the card views that previously lacked them, while views that already supported the styling were left unchanged.

items.s: Android OCR scan - migrate to Jetpack Compose
items.w: Migrated the Android OCR scan screen to Jetpack Compose as part of modernizing the app's UI toolkit.
items.y: Part of modernizing the Android app's UI stack onto Jetpack Compose.
items.o: OCR scan feature migrated to Jetpack Compose.

items.s: [BE test] API test: Basket Add validation incorrectly rejects valid itemId values
items.w: Fixed a basket validation bug that wrongly rejected valid equipment/event/ticket item IDs, which could have blocked legitimate purchases.
items.y: This validation bug could block legitimate purchases; the corresponding tests were failing and needed a real fix.
items.o: Basket 'add' validation now correctly accepts valid item IDs across equipment, event, and ticket types.

items.s: [BE test] API test: IndividualPaymentCest returns 403 instead of 400 for missing paymentTo validation
items.w: Fixed the payment checkout API to return a proper 400 validation error, instead of a misleading 403, when paymentTo is missing.
items.y: Incorrect error codes make it harder for clients/integrators to handle checkout errors correctly.
items.o: Missing paymentTo now correctly returns a 400 validation error.

items.s: [BE test] API test: TicketingSettingsCest: Fatal OOM in error handling loop when SQS fails
items.w: Fixed a fatal OOM crash caused by infinite recursion in error-notification handling when the SQS queue is unavailable.
items.y: This was a stability risk: any error combined with SQS being down could bring down a request with an OOM crash rather than a normal error response.
items.o: Error handling no longer recurses infinitely when SQS fails; endpoints return proper error responses instead of crashing.

items.s: [BE test] API test: Auth endpoint does not resolve country or isCountryFixed flag
items.w: Fixed the auth endpoint to correctly return a user's resolved country and isCountryFixed flag instead of blank/false values.
items.y: Downstream logic and UI likely depend on these fields being correct to apply country-specific behavior.
items.o: Auth endpoint now correctly resolves and returns country and isCountryFixed.
