items.s: iOS/ Ids
items.w: Catalogued ~170 Android Maestro test identifiers for iOS to implement, enabling cross-platform automated E2E test coverage.
items.y: Needed to bring iOS to parity with Android's automated UI testing coverage.
items.o: Produced a verified list of roughly 170 identifiers (164 confirmed against Android resources, 1 needing explicit iOS implementation, 2 skipped as work-in-progress) for iOS to implement.

items.s: Implementing Universal Pagination Memory in Admin Panel for User Experience Enhancement - Good To Have List ONLY
items.w: Admin Panel lists remember each user's page, page size and sorting after a refresh or on returning, alongside the filters they already remembered.
items.y: A customer reported that refreshing or returning reset lists to page one, losing their place in long lists.
items.o: Organisers come back to exactly the view they left on participants, exhibitors, sessions and other lists.

items.s: [BE Test fail] Import Participants: DataController sync path swallows $account->save() failures
items.w: Fixed exhibitor-scoped participant imports silently reporting success even when accounts failed to save.
items.y: Surfaced by a previously-skipped end-to-end test revealing a false-positive success signal with real data-loss risk.
items.o: Fix identified to check each save's return value and aggregate per-row failures into the response so the reported count reflects only actually-persisted participants.

items.s: [BE Test fail] Import Participants: missing save-failure guard in ImportTask::importVisitorAction causes invalid PHQL and stale cron_task
items.w: Fixed a bad participant row crashing the import worker and leaving the job stuck re-failing forever instead of being skipped.
items.y: Surfaced by a previously-skipped end-to-end test showing a real production reliability risk (stuck imports, log floods, unbounded queue growth).
items.o: Fix identified to log the failed row, skip it, and continue processing rather than crashing and leaving a stale queued job.

items.s: [BE Test fail] Import Participants: ImportTask::getBlockFormData TypeError aborts worker on null getFormDataAssoc()
items.w: Fixed one misconfigured custom field crashing the entire participant-import batch instead of just the affected row.
items.y: Surfaced by a previously-skipped end-to-end test revealing that one misconfigured field on an event could break imports for every organiser using that event.
items.o: Fix identified to default the unresolved block to an empty array so only the affected row is impacted, not the whole batch.

items.s: Expand non-mutual likes into mutual likes
items.w: Adds configurable preprocessing to the matchmaking engine that expands one-sided likes into mutual likes for specified role directions, improving meeting/speed-networking schedule coverage.
items.y: Product Vision — increases matchmaking flexibility and meeting yield for events that need denser schedules.
items.o: An API-configurable preprocessing step that transforms one-sided likes into mutual-like pairs per role direction before scheduling.

items.s: Generate additional pairs or meetings without existing likes
items.w: Adds a mechanism to generate additional mutual-like pairs between users who have no existing likes, increasing meeting schedule coverage where demand signals are sparse.
items.y: Product Vision — raises schedule density and utilization for matchmaking-driven events.
items.o: A configurable pre/post-processing mechanism that generates additional mutual-like pairs (per-user caps or timeslot-based) while respecting existing restrictions.

items.s: Boost performance with ApiCache::get()
items.w: Makes ApiCache::get() actually read the response cache, so exhibitor API endpoints stop missing a cache they already write to and respond faster.
items.y: Identified as the highest-leverage single change across the Exhibitor API surface and a prerequisite to measuring other endpoint improvements.
items.o: The cache read path is implemented in get(), so endpoints that already write correct cache keys with a 1-hour TTL can serve cached responses.

items.s: Remove components/layouts/LoaderPlug.tsx and reuse expo-react-components LoaderPlug
items.w: Replaces the duplicate LoaderPlug in portal-ui with the shared expo-react-components version, giving one consistent loading component.
items.y: The shared component should be the single source of truth for loading states.
items.o: All 20+ portal-ui callers import the shared LoaderPlug, props are reconciled, the local file is deleted and typecheck, lint and loading-state smoke tests pass.

items.s: Organizer Platform: Superadmin can configure Burger Menu Footer Logo in App Builder so that mobile apps can show ExpoPlatform (or custom) branding consistently
items.w: Adds a Superadmin-only App Builder toggle, on by default, that shows an ExpoPlatform logo under the app version in the mobile burger menu.
items.y: Lets ExpoPlatform display its branding consistently in mobile apps while Superadmins keep control per event.
items.o: A per-event 'Burger menu footer logo' setting visible only to Superadmins; the backend passes the flag so iOS and Android show or hide the logo.

items.s: Remove "newfront" in the url
items.w: Backend tracking story for removing the legacy '/newfront' path segment from URLs as part of the New Front migration, cleaning up legacy routing and technical debt.
items.y: Platform Health — mirrors the Engineering Innovation New Front migration epic to retire legacy routing in the backend.
items.o: Backend analysis and tracking toward removing '/newfront' from routing/config while keeping existing pages and APIs working (acceptance criteria pending backend impact analysis).

items.s: Admin panel rearangement. Move Sponsorship
items.w: Sponsorship becomes a top-level Admin Panel menu item right after Management, and a standalone module in Module Management.
items.y: Sponsorship is a standalone, revenue-generating module and deserves its own place in the menu.
items.o: Organisers find sponsorship at the top level, with existing on/off states and functionality unchanged.

items.s: Auto login after logout when personate was used
items.w: Fixes a bug where, after using impersonation in the admin panel, logging out of another account silently logs the user back in as the first account.
items.y: Unexpected auto-login into the wrong account is a security and trust risk.
items.o: Logout after impersonation is to end the session cleanly without re-authenticating as the previously impersonated account.

items.s: Fix work with local and session storages in case they are disabled
items.w: Fixed a production crash in Android WebViews where disabled DOM storage caused the app to throw on every storage write.
items.y: Directly caused by a real production error report from Android WebViews.
items.o: New storage-availability checks correctly detect SSR, null storage, and SecurityError cases across all 8 affected storage methods, with 3 call sites that bypassed the shared helper migrated to use it, preserving existing null/no-op behaviour.

items.s: Transfer admin notifications to the SQS queue
items.w: Gave admin notifications their own SQS queue so they no longer wait behind unrelated jobs, fixing a delay bug traced to shared-queue contention.
items.y: Root-caused during investigation of a specific admin-notification delay incident (EP-53422); fixing the shared-queue contention was identified as the direct remedy.
items.o: A dedicated SQS queue with its own worker concurrency/scaling and monitoring now handles admin notification dispatch, isolating it from general workload contention.

items.s: Add detailed CloudWatch logging for Campaign sender list generation process
items.w: Added full CloudWatch observability to campaign sender-list generation so the next stuck-campaign incident can be diagnosed instead of guessed at.
items.y: Directly prioritised as a follow-up to close the observability gap that blocked diagnosis of EP-52933.
items.o: CloudWatch now captures job start/completion, recipient counts per step, errors/unexpected states, and duration/performance metrics for sender-list generation.

items.s: Extend duplicate send protection for Campaign emails beyond 24-hour window
items.w: Closes a gap where campaign recipients could still receive a duplicate email after more than 24 hours, protecting sender trust and recipient experience.
items.y: Surfaced during investigation of a related duplicate-send incident (EP-52621), which showed the existing time-bounded dedup logic has a gap.
items.o: A deduplication strategy is being designed and implemented to guarantee no duplicate send regardless of elapsed time, covering resend and recipient-group-change edge cases.

items.s: [TechDept] Optimize memory usage during Payments export
items.w: Optimises memory usage during Payments export (ticket had no further detail).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; tagged as tech debt.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; reduced memory use for the Payments export is planned.

items.s: Restoring Google Analytics Support: Enhancements for GA4 Integration and Validation
items.w: Google Analytics works again with GA4: the admin ID field validates the G- format, flags old UA IDs, and the site loads GA4 with the saved ID.
items.y: Neither Universal Analytics nor GA4 was working on the platform.
items.o: Organisers track their event website in GA4; nothing loads when the ID is empty or invalid.

items.s: Align Contact Details block to the canonical rule on iOS and Android
items.w: Makes Contact Details the first content block on every profile type in the iOS and Android apps, with the same rows in the same order and no duplicated values.
items.y: Design decided a canonical rule so profiles look and behave identically across People and Scanned Badges on both platforms.
items.o: Contact Details sits first after the header with email, website, personal phone and social rows; empty rows or blocks are hidden and company data stays in Additional Information.

items.s: Email pipeline reliability: per-client isolation, stream split (transactional vs marketing), input validation, rate-limit kill-switch
items.w: Hardens the email pipeline so one client's bounces cannot stop email for everyone, with separate transactional and marketing streams, validation and scoped kill-switches.
items.y: Stakeholders report significant revenue loss from platform-wide email shutdowns and view email delivery as essential.
items.o: Planned: split transactional and marketing streams on separate SES identities, per-client isolation, validation of addresses before SES, and a per-client-scoped kill-switch.

items.s: Google Analytics field front-end validation
items.w: Adds front-end format validation, placeholder and help text to the Google Analytics (GA4) ID field in the Admin Panel, while still allowing an empty value to disable tracking.
items.y: Customer Request — part of restoring GA support; prevents misconfiguration of GA4 tracking by organizers.
items.o: The GA ID input now validates the GA4 format (G-XXXXXXXXXX), shows placeholder and help text warning against duplicate GA injection, and permits an empty value to clear tracking.

items.s: Researching access logic
items.w: Mapped the platform's existing category/networking-permission rules onto global search so an opted-out or restricted user never shows up in someone else's results.
items.y: A foundational requirement for the AI-powered Search Anatomy initiative — search cannot ship without correctly inheriting the platform's existing visibility rules.
items.o: Documented how the layered visibility model (permission matrix, networking opt-in/GDPR, connection settings, module toggles) must be applied when filtering global search results.

items.s: Researching new entities for search
items.w: Scoped which of the platform's 13+ content types (exhibitors, sessions, products, news, groups and more) the new search feature needs to eventually cover.
items.y: Needed to define the full scope of entities the AI-powered Search Anatomy initiative must support before broader implementation.
items.o: Defined the target list of 13+ entity types (Exhibitors, Visitors, Hosted Buyers, Speakers, Sessions, Products, News, Brands, Pavilions, Round Tables, On-Demand, Groups, etc.) search must eventually cover.

items.s: Enable filtering on DS side for marketplace filters
items.w: Marketplace filters are applied on the data-science search side, so search results come back already filtered by the active filters.
items.y: So searching on the marketplace respects the filters the user has applied.
items.o: Search and filters work together on marketplace listings.

items.s: HOTFIX: Add temporary caching for /api/session/basket/list requests in mobile apps
items.w: Adds temporary client-side caching of /api/session/basket/list in the mobile apps to cut the duplicate traffic seen during IMEX.
items.y: An immediate hotfix was needed to reduce backend load and stabilise production traffic while a larger refactor is planned.
items.o: A TTL-based cache (1–5 minutes) keyed by user, event and parameters, with in-flight de-duplication and refresh on session-related changes.

items.s: Admin notifications: hybrid idempotency (DB UNIQUE + post-FCM Redis flag)
items.w: Makes admin notification sending retry-safe with a DB unique constraint and a post-FCM Redis flag, so users get neither duplicate pushes nor missed ones.
items.y: Removes the accepted trade-off from EP-53440 between duplicate pushes and silent delivery loss.
items.o: A UNIQUE index with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING protects in-app records, and a per-user Redis flag set after successful FCM dispatch skips only users already notified.

items.s: Front-end for chatbot
items.w: Builds the redesigned chatbot front end in the Admin Panel (ExpoAssistant) using the Untitled UI library, wired to Data Science endpoints, as the v1 UI for the platform's AI assistant.
items.y: Product Vision — delivers the customer-facing UI layer for the AI assistant (ExpoAssistant) on the Admin Panel.
items.o: A redesigned chatbot front end built to the Figma prototype and connected to DS-provided endpoints (v1 excludes like/dislike feedback).

items.s: Layout refactor
items.w: Refactors the frontend layout (ticket had no further detail).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; a layout refactor is planned.

items.s: Fix notistack colors.
items.w: Fixed toast notification colors to use the design system's static CSS variables instead of ad hoc theme values, per the official Figma spec.
items.y: Design-system compliance fix flagged against the official Figma design spec.
items.o: Notistack styling is updated to use static, CSS-variable-based colors matching the design system (e.g. Functional/Focus tokens).

items.s: Investigate New Architecture and Registration Flow
items.w: Investigation/discovery story defining the Registration microservice within the monolith-to-microservices transition — its domain boundaries, APIs, events, integration points and migration approach.
items.y: Product Vision — foundational architecture investigation enabling the platform's move to a microservices-oriented, scalable architecture.
items.o: A defined scope for the Registration microservice (responsibilities, APIs, events, data, integration points, observability and migration strategy) to guide extraction from the monolith.

items.s: Remove legacy "-next14" branches
items.w: Renames the frontend repo branches so the live Next.js 14 branches take the canonical names and the old v12 branches are kept as -next12 legacy.
items.y: Next.js 14 is now the live production version, so its branches should be the default and the confusion removed.
items.o: v12 branches renamed to -next12, v14 branches renamed to master/alpha/rc/hotFix/prod, with DevOps reconfiguring the prod build trigger and branch permissions.

items.s: Migrate i18next to the ICU format
items.w: Migrated the front-end i18n stack to a unified ICU MessageFormat with stable dotted keys, laying the foundation for reliable translation tooling across all repos.
items.y: Parent tech-debt initiative to unify translation infrastructure so it can support reliable tooling, linting, and vendor translation workflows going forward.
items.o: Migrated to i18next-icu with single-brace ICU placeholders, ICU plural/select blocks, named Trans tags, and stable dotted-ID keys, with lint tooling and a CI gate.

items.s: Post-incident review and RCA
items.w: Produces a post-incident review and root cause analysis of the compromised AWS keys incident, with prevention, detection and response actions.
items.y: Security incident response: understand how the leak happened and stop it recurring.
items.o: A Confluence RCA with timeline, scope, 5 Whys, action items for prevention, detection and response, and an updated secret-hygiene policy for dev onboarding.

items.s: Make Exhibitor module with CREATE command
items.w: Replaced 30+ scattered, duplicated places that create Exhibitor records with one tested, documented CREATE module, reducing risk across the whole codebase.
items.y: Part of the Implement Exhibitor CRUD epic to consolidate a business-critical, heavily-duplicated code path into one governed, tested module.
items.o: A unified Exhibitor CREATE command with documentation, Swagger, unit test coverage, and performance/security/penetration review.

items.s: [admin-ui] Change docker node to 24
items.w: Unified admin-ui's Docker images onto a single Node 24 version across every build stage, removing a latent source of ABI/runtime mismatches.
items.y: Routine infrastructure hygiene to remove an inconsistency that could cause subtle, hard-to-trace runtime bugs.
items.o: All three admin-ui Dockerfiles now use node:24-alpine consistently across every build stage, verified to build and run correctly.

items.s: Android: menu refactoring
items.w: Refactored the Android app's menu module (parsing, display, prep logic) for better maintainability; ticket gives no further detail on scope.
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

items.s: Rework integration activation
items.w: Reworks integration activation so an active subscription alone controls data flow, removing the redundant Enable Exhibitor and Enable Visitor checkboxes.
items.y: The old checkbox no longer had a real purpose and created confusing, inconsistent behaviour.
items.o: Creating a subscription activates the integration; pausing or deleting it stops data flow, and the enable checkboxes are removed.

items.s: Remove Unconfirmed Appointment email template
items.w: Removed a leftover email template from a retired Hosted Buyer meeting feature that had no remaining use, decluttering the admin templates screen.
items.y: Routine cleanup identified as having no remaining use or value.
items.o: The unused email template is removed from Networking & Matchmaking > Meetings > Email Templates.

items.s: portal-ui: clean up unused files in public/ and dead Meta/PagePlug/ErrorsPageControl/HomePageController chain
items.w: Cleaned out dead legacy assets and a whole unused SEO/error-page component chain left behind by the App Router migration, verified file-by-file for safety.
items.y: The App Router's own route files (manifest, icon, error, not-found) now cover everything the old chain did, so it is redundant dead weight in the repo.
items.o: Removes a defined list of unused public assets (icons, demo images, unused SVGs) and the dead Meta/PagePlug/ErrorsPageControl/HomePageController component chain, including associated Redux entries and tests.

items.s: Summary Support dynamic Firebase signing key configuration for client-published mobile apps
items.w: Supports multiple Firebase signing keys for client-published mobile apps so deep links work when apps are signed under client accounts.
items.y: More apps are being published directly under client accounts, so signing configuration must handle this reliably.
items.o: Firebase configs and assetlinks.json support the correct fingerprints for all apps, deep links work, push impact is investigated and the setup flow is documented.

items.s: Global Search. Sponsored Exhibitors
items.w: A rotating Sponsored Exhibitors card on the Global Search page, with the organiser's label, sponsor bar colour, arrows and sponsor sorting rules.
items.y: To give sponsors an additional promotion surface on the new search page.
items.o: Sponsors rotate every five seconds regardless of the query, and views and clicks count in the same statistics as the marketplace.

items.s: Global Search. Sponsored Products
items.w: A rotating Sponsored Products block on the Global Search page, with a configurable label, sponsor colour, arrows and product sorting rules.
items.y: To give sponsors' products an additional promotion surface on the new search page.
items.o: Sponsored products rotate on the search page, respect visibility restrictions, and feed the same product statistics as the marketplace.

items.s: [Tech] Make Product module
items.w: Builds the new Product module on a modular DDD + CQRS hexagonal architecture under /src, establishing the foundation and patterns for migrating further modules off the legacy Phalcon monolith.
items.y: Platform Health — sets the architectural foundation (SharedKernel, Platform, Modules, command/query buses, v3 API base) for ongoing monolith decomposition.
items.o: A Product module implemented on a three-tier modular architecture with command/query buses, shared kernel value objects, DI over Phalcon, and a Public API v3 base — the reusable template for future module migrations.

items.s: [DS Spike] Post-filtering prototype: merge Qdrant results against allowed ID vector
items.w: Benchmarked merging AI search results against permission-allowed ID lists at scale, to prove out one candidate approach for secure AI search.
items.y: Needed to validate a candidate architecture for enforcing per-user visibility/permission rules in the new AI-powered search before committing to it.
items.o: A prototype measuring merge latency across allowed-ID-vector sizes (1k-100k) and result-set sizes (10-99% of records), with documented performance thresholds and a production recommendation.

items.s: [DS Spike] Pre-filtering evaluation: pass allowed ID vector as Qdrant filter condition
items.w: Tested passing permission-allowed IDs as a Qdrant pre-filter versus post-filtering, to settle which approach AI search should use in production.
items.y: A direct comparison baseline is needed against the post-filtering spike (EP-53900) to decide the production architecture for permission-aware AI search.
items.o: Pre-filtering implemented and benchmarked across allowed-ID-vector sizes (1k-100k), producing a latency comparison table and a production recommendation vs post-filtering.

items.s: [Exhibitor Spike] Design API to provide allowed entity ID vector per search category with security and filter context
items.w: Designed the Exhibitor-backend API that will supply AI search with the exact set of entity IDs each user is permitted to see, per category.
items.y: A required building block for permission-aware AI search, coordinated with the DS team's post/pre-filtering spikes (EP-53900, EP-53902).
items.o: A proposed API design (endpoint, request/response schema, expected max size per category, V1-scoped security/filter rules) documented and shared with the DS team for review.

items.s: [Spike] Define AI Search ↔ Exhibitor backend communication protocol for allowed ID vector request
items.w: Nailed down the exact request/response contract between AI Search and the Exhibitor backend for fetching a user's allowed entity IDs, unblocking both teams.
items.y: Needed to unblock parallel implementation by DS and Exhibitor teams on the permission-aware AI search architecture (related to EP-53900, EP-53903).
items.o: Agreed and documented request/response schema, edge-case behaviour (no filters, full access, unauthenticated), published in Confluence with sign-off from both teams.

items.s: Optimize get session flow on session page
items.w: Optimises how the sessions page loads so visitors and search engines see sessions for the nearest date immediately instead of an initial 'no sessions' state.
items.y: The empty first render harms SEO and user perception of the agenda.
items.o: An agreed approach, either a nearest-date sessions endpoint or separate dates and sessions requests, lets the page render sessions on first load.

items.s: Improve Exhibitor APIs
items.w: Improves the Exhibitor APIs as part of the Exhibitor CRUD work (ticket had no further detail).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; part of the Implement Exhibitor CRUD epic.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

items.s: Update on Team Member Creation Rules for Exhibitors and Login Uniqueness Validation
items.w: Creating team members and other users now checks for duplicate logins, not duplicate emails, with a clear 'already used as a login' error.
items.y: Exhibitors were wrongly blocked from adding a team member whose email matched another exhibitor's contact email.
items.o: Legitimate team members can be created, duplicate logins are still prevented, and the rule is the same in admin, portal and API.

items.s: Enhancing Meetings report and Custom Meeting Wizard Report: Adding Business Transaction Likelihood and Meeting Did Not Take Place Columns
items.w: The Meetings report and Custom Meeting Wizard report gain Business Transaction Likelihood (0–10) and Meeting Did Not Take Place columns.
items.y: Organisers of meeting-focused events need all rating data to judge event success; these fields were tracked but not exported.
items.o: Exports include both columns for every rated meeting, including ratings submitted before the release.

items.s: Enhancing Privacy for Opted-Out Users: Favouriting Features and GDPR Compliance
items.w: Opted-out attendees can favourite users, exhibitors and products privately; these favourites never expose them, count as leads or appear in the API.
items.y: Attendees want to bookmark content while keeping full control of their data under strict GDPR expectations, especially in Germany.
items.o: Favouriting works for everyone on web and app; counters note they may include anonymous favourites, and privacy holds if users later opt in.

items.s: Make Table Meetings supports the date range outside the 1970–2037
items.w: Stops the Table Meetings list crashing on dates outside 1970–2037 by guarding input and widening how dates are stored.
items.y: A scheduling platform cannot have its meetings list fail for dates after 2037.
items.o: A frontend guard prevents the crash, and migration to bigint timestamps is recommended to support any realistic date range.

items.s: [TechDept] Export finalize must not rely on exact total-count match — add explicit batch tracker

items.s: Remove duplicated requests for banners, in case they are not added at all
items.w: Stopped the frontend from re-firing the same empty banner request on every navigation, cutting wasted API calls for placements with no banners configured.
items.y: Diagnosed from a recorded session (Jam) showing three identical redundant requests within seven seconds on a live event's marketplace listing.
items.o: Empty-result caching stops re-requesting banners for empty placements within a session, while still picking up newly-added banners via TTL/reload, without affecting placements that do have banners.

items.s: Convert admin panel ICU keys to the snake_case

items.o: ~2,631 English and ~1,158 Russian keys across 47 namespaces renamed to snake_case, with all ~921 referencing source files updated in the same change; ICU values stay byte-identical.

items.s: Restrict meetings and messages with exhibitors with no team members
items.w: Brought mobile in line with web by blocking meeting/message requests to exhibitors with no team members, removing a manual pre-launch organizer check.
items.y: Closes a long-standing web/mobile feature parity gap and removes a manual, error-prone organizer workaround.
items.o: Meet/Message buttons on mobile are greyed out with an explanatory toast and accessibility labels when an exhibitor has zero eligible team members, applied consistently across profile, listing, matchmaking, and chat-initiation surfaces.

items.s: AI Search: implement post-filtering by allowed ID list
items.w: AI semantic search can now be constrained to an allowed list of entity IDs, so applied filters and search relevance work together instead of conflicting.
items.y: Scalability Initiative following spike EP-53552 and a DS team decision: a stateless post-filtering design lets the backend resolve filters to IDs and the search service rank only within that set, a reusable pattern across ~40 filters.
items.o: The AI search API accepts an optional allowed_ids parameter and applies it as a pre-search constraint in Qdrant, so results satisfy both semantic relevance and the active filters, with no regression when the list is absent.

items.s: AI Search: add pagination support (offset + frame size)
items.w: AI search results are now paginated, letting users browse beyond the first page of semantic results without re-running the whole search.
items.y: Scalability Initiative agreed in the DS team meeting: a stateless offset/frame_size approach delivers pagination quickly, with stable-pagination caching deliberately deferred.
items.o: The AI search API accepts offset and frame_size parameters and returns the correct Qdrant ranking window, combining correctly with allowed_ids filtering.

items.s: N+1 query loop in By Booking report (SessionOrdersRepository)

items.s: [X-1] Cross-cutting infra: parallelism + HTTP + logging
items.w: Sets up the shared test infrastructure in the PHP stack: parallel runs, HTTP clients and redacted logging, replacing the teststone equivalents.
items.y: Part of migrating Integration-team tests from teststone into the PHP backend (Codeception/Pest) and e2e-testing.
items.o: Parallel runner via robo-paracept or Pest --parallel, HTTP via Guzzle/Codeception REST, and Monolog with an OTel handler and redaction, with parallelism gated on H2.

items.s: [X-2] Test-data seeding migration
items.w: Migrates teststone's test-data seeding to the PHP stack, choosing a seeding approach and porting the 126 dataset specs and their discipline.
items.y: Part of migrating Integration-team tests from teststone into the PHP backend (Codeception/Pest) and e2e-testing.
items.o: DatasetSpecs audited as static (nelmio/alice) or dynamic (PHP orchestrator), a seeding primitive chosen, worker-band IDs mapped to tenants, and hub and module-flag seeders ported.

items.s: [X-3] Observability / Grafana carry-forward
items.w: Keeps the five Grafana test dashboards and two alert rules working after the test migration by re-emitting the same metrics from PHP OpenTelemetry.
items.y: Preserves test observability through the teststone to PHP migration.
items.o: PHP OTel emits the same metric names and labels, the 5 dashboards keep rendering, the 2 alert rules are recalibrated after 14 days and the Vitest emitter retires.

items.s: Introduce a centralized locale-aware navigation layer (router + links)
items.w: Built a locale-aware navigation layer that removes an extra redirect on every non-English page view and fixes ~8 broken locale-naive comparisons across the app.
items.y: Surfaced while fixing an infinite invite redirect loop (EP-54331), where a locale-naive comparison escalated a harmless extra redirect into an infinite loop; a full 111-file code audit showed the pattern is widespread.
items.o: A drop-in locale-aware router and link wrapper (with lint guards banning the raw APIs) eliminate the extra redirect on non-default locales, and a locale-neutral route-matching utility fixes the ~8 broken comparisons (scroll control, header search, auth modal, nav highlighting, etc.).

items.s: Investigate and remove unused SignInPageController (dead code with latent locale redirect-loop)
items.w: Investigated and removed an unused sign-in component that carried a latent infinite-redirect-loop bug, before it could ever resurface in production.
items.y: Sibling cleanup task to the centralized locale-aware navigation work, closing off a latent bug before it can resurface.
items.o: The component is confirmed unused and removed entirely, or — if still required — re-wired with a locale-safe guard, verified not to loop on non-default locales.

items.s: Show event name in admin notifications title
items.w: Shows the event name as the title of admin push notifications instead of the generic 'Event Message', so attendees know which event a message is from.
items.y: Organisers need attendees to understand event context immediately, without opening the app.
items.o: All admin-initiated pushes, including test messages sent from Marketing → Admin Notifications, use the event name from Event settings as the title.

items.s: Refactor expo-react-components ICU translation keys to the snake_case
items.w: Renamed the shared component library's translation keys to snake_case, closing the last inconsistency in the platform's unified i18n key convention.
items.y: Removes the last inconsistency in the platform's i18n key convention now that admin-ui and next14 are both snake_case.
items.o: ~103 keys across 16 locale files renamed to snake_case, all ~42 call sites and the docs/skill files updated, with ICU values left byte-identical.

items.s: [Admin Redesign] Event list
items.w: The admin Event List page is being restyled to the modern Untitled UI design language as part of the Phase 1 admin redesign.
items.y: Part of the Admin Redesign initiative (Phase 1, 5 core pages) to modernise the admin panel incrementally.
items.o: Untitled UI CSS restyling of the Event List admin page, consistent with the other Phase 1 pages; specific details are not documented in the ticket.

items.s: [Dashboard] [/Splitted : Part 2] UX/UI new Event Reporting dashboards are embedded as a new sub-section under the existing Analytics module
items.w: Six more automated Event Reporting dashboards (Exhibitor Analytics, Platform Performance, Mobile App, and more) were added as an Analytics sub-section.
items.y: Product Vision / self-service reporting — part of the Automated Event Reporting Dashboards epic delivering Embeddable.com-powered dashboards so organisers get deeper insight without bespoke reports.
items.o: Six additional Embeddable.com dashboards were embedded as a new sub-section under the existing Analytics module, sitting alongside (not replacing) the current analytics pages in the organiser admin navigation.

items.s: AI Tools Investigation / Creation
items.w: Explores AI tools and builds automations to speed up the design team's routine tasks.
items.y: Internal efficiency: help the design team work faster.
items.o: Available AI tools are investigated and, where it makes sense, custom automations are built for design processes.

items.s: Add pagination to native floorplan
items.w: Adds independent pagination to the Exhibition and Conference Halls lists on the Floor Plan admin screen and loads availability times only when a hall is edited.
items.y: Keeps the Admin Panel performant for large-scale events during setup.
items.o: Each hall list has its own 'On page' selector (default 12) and page controls, and availability times are fetched only when editing a specific hall.

items.s: [Spike] Do the load testing on ID preparations
items.w: Load-tested whether the database can generate 100k-ID permission lists across 16 categories at once without buckling, de-risking AI search before full build-out.
items.y: A prerequisite risk check before committing to full implementation of the AI Search permission-scoping pipeline.
items.o: A PHP test endpoint applies GDPR/permission logic to fetch IDs from a prod-like database, measuring DB connection time and Redis footprint to validate the approach can handle production scale.

items.s: Migrate trial test plan to e2e repository
items.w: The Integration team's trial test plans for Event Statistics and Session Program were migrated from teststone into the e2e testing repository.
items.y: Technical Debt / Maintenance — executing the Test Automation Strategy to migrate Integration-team tests off teststone into the standard e2e repository as the single source of truth.
items.o: Trial test plans and supporting docs for Event Statistics and Session Program were moved into the e2e repository, with updates now made only there and tests re-classified and re-levelled.

items.s: Fix intermittently failing (flaky) tests
items.w: Fixed flaky unit tests caused by asserting on content before it finished rendering asynchronously, restoring trust in the CI test suite.
items.y: Flaky tests block reliable CI signal and waste engineering time re-running or investigating false failures.
items.o: Synchronous assertions on asynchronously-rendered content are replaced with findBy/waitFor, and affected post/feed tests are audited for missing awaits and test isolation issues.

items.s: Onboarding Flow
items.w: Delivers the multi-step organiser onboarding journey that captures profile, event details and event goals and saves them to the platform.
items.y: Part of Organizer Onboarding v1, helping new organisers set up events themselves.
items.o: Screens for pre-filled profile, editable event details with auto timezone and date and file validation, and multi-select goals and event type, all saved to the event.

items.s: Admin Panel (Event Setup Screen) Redesign
items.w: Lets a TAM create an event within an approved customer environment, with mandatory fields enforced, as the starting point for organiser onboarding.
items.y: Part of Organizer Onboarding v1; the event must exist before the organiser can be onboarded.
items.o: An 'Add New Event' flow with clearly marked mandatory fields blocks progress until they are complete and lands the TAM on the Event Dashboard after saving.

items.s: Email Flow
items.w: Lets a TAM send a one-time onboarding email to an organiser admin, whose link opens the first screen of the onboarding journey.
items.y: Part of Organizer Onboarding v1, kicking off self-service event setup.
items.o: A 'Send Onboarding Email' option and popup with send or skip appear for the first admin user, disappear after use, and the email link redirects to Screen 1.

items.s: Dashboard
items.w: Lands organisers on an Event Dashboard after onboarding, showing real-time attendee, exhibitor, session, speaker and lead counts.
items.y: Part of Organizer Onboarding v1, giving organisers immediate value after setup.
items.o: The dashboard shows registered and checked-in attendees, exhibitors, sessions, speakers and total leads, plus Team Members and Selected Modules widgets.

items.s: Android/ Pls update FllorPlan behaviour
items.w: Fixed the Android app so it stops showing the ExpoFP floor plan after an organizer disables it, instead of only reacting to a separate dynamic-linking toggle.
items.y: Reported behaviour mismatch between the organizer's configured setting and what the app actually displays.
items.o: App behaviour is updated so the floor plan display correctly reflects the organizer's current ExpoFP setting.

items.s: Open T&Cs in new browser
items.w: During mobile registration, tapping Terms of Use now opens it in the device's external browser instead of hijacking the registration web-view.
items.y: Prioritised via product discovery (PBV11-378) to remove a progress-loss friction point in the revenue-adjacent mobile registration flow.
items.o: On both iOS and Android, the Terms of Use link opens in an external browser without disturbing the current registration screen, and returning users find their progress intact.

items.s: Add sorting to floorplan in mobile
items.w: Groups the mobile floorplan bottom sheet with exhibitors first and sessions second, each sorted alphabetically, matching the web experience.
items.y: Aligns the mobile floorplan with the web and improves usability during the live event.
items.o: On iOS and Android the bottom sheet lists exhibitors by company name, then sessions by title, both alphabetically.

items.s: App-side verification: exhibitor logo gating in mobile sync (null logo when disabled)
items.w: Verifies that the mobile apps handle the new null exhibitor logo in sync, showing a placeholder when an exhibitor's logo setting is disabled.
items.y: Follow-up to EP-47975, which made the logo an exhibitor setting controlled per category or exhibitor.
items.o: iOS and Android are checked for placeholder rendering, pick-up of disable and re-enable, local cache clearing and the category-change delta sync case.

items.s: [Exhibitor Settings] Tech debt: avoid N+1 when resolving exhibitor effective settings in bulk
items.w: Removes an N+1 load pattern when resolving exhibitor effective settings in bulk, such as in mobile sync loops.
items.y: Tech debt that grows with event size and slows sync and list builders.
items.o: Options are resolving from row data already loaded, batched pre-loading, or a category-defaults fast path for simple settings such as logo.

items.s: Tech Debt: Catalogue API contract changes from the pentest/security story (auth)
items.w: Catalogued every API endpoint whose access rules silently changed during the security hardening story and defined a consistent 401/403/404 convention going forward.
items.y: A frontend team already hit confusion from an endpoint 'suddenly requiring a token'; this formalizes what changed across the whole pentest story so it doesn't keep causing surprises.
items.o: A complete list of endpoints with changed access/contract (path, what changed, condition, originating ticket) handed to the frontend team, plus an agreed and documented 401/403/404 convention applied consistently and reflected in Swagger.

items.s: Prepare migration prototype solution
items.w: Prepares a prototype solution for the teststone test migration (ticket had no further detail).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; part of migrating Integration-team tests from teststone to PHP.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; a migration prototype is planned (on hold).

items.s: Android/ Filters unselect after synch arrive
items.w: Fixed the Android app so a background data sync no longer silently clears a user's selected filters on pages like Sessions.
items.y: Reported user-facing frustration from losing filter selections due to an unrelated background process.
items.o: App behaviour is updated to preserve selected filters across a background sync event.

items.s: Native Integration - Swoogo
items.w: A new inbound Swoogo integration automatically syncs registrants, speakers, and exhibitors, deduplicated by company, including cancellations.
items.y: Part of the strategic Integration Hub programme to expand EP's native connector ecosystem and remove onboarding friction for clients on third-party registration platforms.
items.o: In progress: a polled, OAuth2, external-ID-matched inbound integration with four flows (account and exhibitor set/delete), team-member matching, delta cursors, and full field mappings, running on the Integration Hub AutoUpdate engine.

items.s: Story 1. Main Participant registration page setup
items.w: Organisers can set up the Participant registration welcome page in the Admin Panel: hero image, title and description, each switchable, with a flip-sides layout.
items.y: So attendees arriving at registration get a branded first impression that matches the event.
items.o: The registration landing page shows the organiser's image and multilingual welcome text, with save, cancel and unsaved-changes warnings in setup.

items.s: Story 2. Main Buyer registration page setup
items.w: Organisers can set up the Buyer registration welcome page: hero image, title and description, each switchable, with a flip-sides layout.
items.y: So buyers arriving via a shared link see branded imagery and a welcome that matches the event.
items.o: Buyer registration opens on a branded, multilingual welcome page configured in the Admin Panel.

items.s: Story 3. Confirmation page setup for Participant
items.w: Organisers can configure the Participant confirmation page: image, title, rich-text description with merge variables, an optional script, or a custom Website Builder page.
items.y: So participants see a branded page confirming registration with personal details such as name, email and badge links.
items.o: After registering, participants land on a personalised confirmation page with values like name, QR code and print-badge link filled in.

items.s: Story 4. Confirmation page setup for Buyer
items.w: Organisers can configure the Buyer confirmation page: image, title, rich-text description with merge variables, an optional script, or a custom Website Builder page.
items.y: So buyers see a branded page confirming registration with their personal details and badge links.
items.o: Buyers land on a personalised confirmation page after registering, set up in the Admin Panel.

items.s: Story 5. Sold out tickets page setup
items.w: Organisers can configure a Sold Out page shown when all registration tickets are gone: image, title, description and a button with a custom link.
items.y: So people trying to register are told tickets are no longer available and guided somewhere useful.
items.o: A branded, multilingual Sold Out page replaces the registration form when tickets run out.

items.s: Story 6. Sold out tickets page
items.w: Participants see the Sold Out page when no tickets remain for them, including when tickets are limited by participant category or country.
items.y: So participants clearly understand registration is closed and can return to the event.
items.o: The Sold Out page appears at the right point in the registration flow, in the chosen language, with a button back to the event.

items.s: Story 7. Registration with payment
items.w: Registration now sends attendees with paid items to the payment page on submit, after an availability check; free registrations complete directly.
items.y: So paid bookings are settled before registration completes.
items.o: Paid items are paid before confirmation; for private events with public access or a reached registration limit, items go to the basket instead.

items.s: Story 8. Registration: Visitor can verify Email on Registration Landing Page
items.w: A registration landing page where visitors enter and verify their email before the Participant registration form, with required and format checks.
items.y: So only valid, unique emails proceed and each visitor is routed to the right flow.
items.o: Duplicate emails are blocked, returning or unfinished registrations are routed to their flows, and closed registration redirects to a set URL.

items.s: Story 9. Registration: Visitor can verify Email on Buyer Registration Landing Page
items.w: A Buyer registration landing page where visitors verify their email before the Buyer form; existing participants confirm identity by email link.
items.y: So only valid, unique emails proceed to Buyer registration and each person follows the correct flow.
items.o: Buyers start with email verification; logged-in participants upgrading to Buyer skip it; existing buyers are blocked from duplicates.

items.s: Story 10. Registration: Remove Simple Registration
items.w: Simple Registration, unused by any customer for years, is removed so the platform keeps a single consistent registration flow.
items.y: Business decision to discontinue an unused legacy option so the platform has one consistent registration flow going into the New Registration rebuild.
items.o: Simple Registration settings, its custom-script hook, and all related UI/logic are removed; every event always goes through the standard Summary-page flow.

items.s: Story 11. Registration: Participant can select and purchase Tickets during Registration
items.w: A mandatory Tickets step in registration where participants pick tickets, limited by category, with availability checks and a one-hour reservation hold.
items.y: So participants secure access to specific dates under their category before completing registration.
items.o: Participants must add a ticket to continue; tickets respect category, visibility and stock rules, and buyers skip the step.

items.s: Story 12. Registration: Condition logic for Grids and Fields during Registration
items.w: Condition logic in the new registration: grids and their fields show or hide by participant category or by the answer to a conditional question.
items.y: So the form adapts to each participant and doesn't ask for information that doesn't apply.
items.o: Hidden grids skip their required fields, empty tabs disappear, and behaviour matches the new Edit Profile.

items.s: Story 13. Tabs navigation
items.w: Tab navigation for the new registration: previous/next buttons, clickable visited tabs, and a side menu with event image, title, tab list and order summary.
items.y: So participants move through the form efficiently, guided by required-field checks and a view of their progress and paid items.
items.o: Registration has a side navigation showing progress and paid items; skipping past unfilled required fields is blocked.

items.s: Story 14. Grids and fields layout
items.w: The new registration uses the Edit Profile grid and field layout, with all field attributes and system fields (email, country, category) pre-filled.
items.y: So registration looks and behaves like the new Edit Profile and respects the organiser's field settings.
items.o: Registration forms honour required, hidden, disabled and conditional fields, keep data between tabs and adapt to screen size.

items.s: Story 15. Sessions as part of Registration
items.w: A Sessions tab in registration where participants browse, search, filter and book paid and free sessions, with 'at least one' or 'all sessions' rules.
items.y: So participants can add sessions to their schedule or order as part of registering.
items.o: Paid sessions go to the order summary, free ones to the schedule, and full sessions are hidden.

items.s: Story 16. Summary
items.w: A Summary step at the end of registration showing submitted details and paid items, with edit links, discount codes, terms and reCAPTCHA.
items.y: So participants can check their data and paid items before paying or submitting.
items.o: Participants review everything in one place and proceed to payment or submit; unavailable required items block completion.

items.s: Story 17. Terms and Conditions
items.w: Terms and Conditions in the new registration: participants view the full text in a pop-up and must agree when the organiser makes it required.
items.y: So organisers can ensure participants accept their terms before registering.
items.o: Registration can't complete until required terms are accepted, matching the old registration.

items.s: Story 18. Email notifications for Registration
items.w: The new registration sends the same emails as the old one: confirmation, pending approval, waiting list and unfinished-registration reminders.
items.y: So participants and organisers keep receiving the same registration communications.
items.o: Organisers' existing email templates and settings work unchanged with the new registration.

items.s: Story 19. Remove Self Registration
items.w: The legacy Self Registration feature is fully removed, leaving one supported registration flow and less code to maintain.
items.y: Cleanup decision to reduce the number of parallel registration code paths ahead of the New Registration rollout.
items.o: Self Registration's Admin Panel settings, frontend pages, and backend logic are removed; legacy URLs redirect appropriately, with no impact to standard, Buyer, or other registration flows.

items.s: Story 20. Embed Participant Category in Registration URLs
items.w: A participant category embedded in the registration URL filters tickets to that category and pre-fills and locks the category field.
items.y: So participants see only relevant options and don't have to pick a category themselves.
items.o: Category-specific registration links work in the new registration, falling back to standard behaviour for invalid categories.

items.s: Story 21. Confirmation page for Participant
items.w: Participants see a confirmation page after registering, with the organiser's image and text, merge variables such as QR code and badge link, and scripts.
items.y: So participants get a personalised confirmation with their details and badge information.
items.o: Every completed registration ends on a multilingual, personalised confirmation page, or the organiser's custom page.

items.s: Story 22. Confirmation page for Buyer
items.w: Buyers see a dedicated confirmation page after Buyer registration, with image, text, merge variables, optional scripts and multilingual content.
items.y: So buyers get a personalised confirmation with their details and badge information.
items.o: Buyer registration ends on a branded confirmation page, or a custom page chosen by the organiser.

items.s: Story 23. Public Registration
items.w: Public registration in the new flow: participants register without organiser approval and activate their profile from the registration email.
items.y: So public events let people register and get access straight away.
items.o: Public-event registration covers email checks, activation, registration limits, repeat and unfinished registrations, and payment.

items.s: Story 24. Registration to Private event with Public access
items.w: Registration for private events with public access: participants submit for approval, paid items are reserved, and payment happens after approval.
items.y: So private events can accept open registrations while the organiser keeps control of who gets in.
items.o: After approval, participants log in to a basket they must pay before their profile becomes active, on web and in the app.

items.s: Story 25. Registration of Buyers
items.w: Buyer registration from an agent's link: buyers register with a new email, submit for organiser approval, and pay reserved items after approval.
items.y: So hosted buyers invited by agents can register while the organiser approves each one.
items.o: Approved buyers pay for reserved items in a basket that can't be closed, then their profile becomes active.

items.s: Story 26. Upgrade from Participant to Buyer
items.w: Existing participants can upgrade to Buyer via an agent's link; their details are pre-filled and the upgrade waits for organiser approval.
items.y: So participants invited as buyers don't have to register again from scratch.
items.o: Logged-in participants go straight to the Buyer form; others confirm by email. They become buyers once the organiser approves.

items.s: Story 27. Registrations with limit
items.w: With a registration limit set, people who register after it's reached join a waiting list and get a waiting-list email instead of an activation link.
items.y: So organisers can control capacity and approve extra registrations themselves.
items.o: Waiting-list registrants can't log in until approved; approved ones activate and pay reserved items in a basket. A modal offers the list if spots run out mid-registration.

items.s: Story 28. Continue unfinished Registration
items.w: Visitors who return with an email that has an unfinished registration can get an email link to resume it, with their earlier answers kept.
items.y: So people don't have to re-enter everything when they come back to finish registering.
items.o: Unfinished registrations can be resumed across all registration types, unless the organiser turns the option off.

items.s: Story 29. Repeated Registration
items.w: Visitors who already have an account from another event confirm by email link and get their standard profile fields pre-filled in the new registration.
items.y: So returning attendees register for a new event faster.
items.o: Repeat registrants see their name, company, position and other system fields filled in and can edit them.

items.s: API front v1: align HTTP 4xx error contract with frontend — stop logging users out on 403/404
items.w: Stops the web frontend logging users out on 403 and 404 errors by agreeing a 4xx contract where only a genuine 401 triggers logout.
items.y: Logged-in users should not lose their session because they hit something forbidden or missing.
items.o: An agreed backend and frontend contract (401 logs out; 400/403/404 show an error), with API front v1 returning semantically correct codes.

items.s: [Invoice&Payments] Search Functionality on Transaction Dashboard and Invoice Payments Pages
items.w: Event admins can now search the Transaction Dashboard and Invoice Payments pages by payer name, surname, or email, replacing manual scrolling.
items.y: Customer-requested out of the RACE 2026 debrief and escalated as a blocker in ACI's renewal discussions, making it a retention priority.
items.o: A search field (name, surname, email) was added above pagination on both the Transaction Dashboard and Invoice Payments pages, querying the Account Name column to locate payment records instantly.

items.s: Migrate remaining test plans to e2e repository
items.w: Test plans are migrated from the legacy teststone repo into the standardized e2e-testing docs structure, one bounded context per PR.
items.y: Continuation of an already-started migration (trial run EP-54579) to consolidate test documentation onto one standard.
items.o: Each bounded context's test plans are migrated (plans only, not implementations) into `docs/tests/bounded-contexts/<context>/` with business.md/product.md/testing.md, removing teststone references, one PR per context.

items.s: Bulk removal of external QR codes
items.w: Lets organisers bulk delete all external QR codes in an event from General > Settings, avoiding attendee data mix-ups when code strings are reused.
items.y: Protects data integrity during event setup.
items.o: A 'Delete QR codes globally' action with double confirmation removes all external QR code strings for the current event only.

items.s: Allow Exhibitor Team Members to View Their Own Exhibitor Profile Regardless of Permission Matrix
items.w: A same-exhibitor bypass fixes a permission-matrix bug that was blocking exhibitor team members from viewing their own company page and colleagues.
items.y: Three confirmed-unintended access scenarios were blocking legitimate same-company access, one of them a regression from an earlier permission fix (EP-50974).
items.o: A same-exhibitor bypass is introduced in the permission-check layer so team members and exhibitor owners can never be blocked from viewing each other or their own company resources, regardless of matrix configuration.

items.s: Resolve overlapping session view from My Schedule in app
items.w: Shows overlapping events side-by-side in My Schedule in the app, with mandatory events first and a '+X more' pill only for four or more overlaps.
items.y: Attendees must always be able to see and open every event on their schedule.
items.o: Two or three overlaps render in equal columns ordered mandatory, then start time, then title; four or more show two cards plus a '+X more' pill.

items.s: Display  Company Name in Interaction Dashboards
items.w: The Interaction Dashboard in participant and exhibitor profiles shows each listed participant's company name, truncated with a tooltip.
items.y: Company names were missing from the interaction dashboards.
items.o: Users can see which company each person they interacted with belongs to.

items.s: Unify rich-editor tag whitelists + replace strip_tags with a real HTML sanitizer (stored-XSS hardening)
items.w: Hardens rich-text fields against stored XSS by replacing strip_tags with a real HTML sanitiser and unifying the drifted tag whitelists.
items.y: Security hardening deferred from the EP-53447 review as project-wide tech debt; no active incident.
items.o: A single shared whitelist and a proper HTML sanitiser applied at all rich-editor call sites.

items.s: Android: Sessions and Exhibitor Events hidden only at the type level should still appear in My Schedule
items.w: Android now shows type-hidden sessions and exhibitor events in My Schedule and reminders, fixing an itinerary gap that iOS never had (IMEX use case).
items.y: Confirmed customer-impacting defect (IMEX) partially reversing an earlier over-broad visibility fix (EP-51214), scoped precisely after QA review.
items.o: Type-level-only hidden Sessions/Exhibitor Events now appear in My Schedule, their detail views, deep links, push notifications/reminders, and calendar export on Android, while item-level hiding and general discovery surfaces remain unchanged.

items.s: Add lang cookie validation
items.w: A malformed language cookie value is now validated and defaulted to English instead of crashing server-side requests, per Grafana error reports.
items.y: Production stability fix to eliminate a class of crash-causing malformed input surfaced in monitoring.
items.o: Language values are validated against the supported list on both client and server before use, with any unknown value degrading gracefully to English instead of crashing the request.

items.s: AI Tools Investigation / Creation (Kristina)
items.w: Investigates or builds AI tools for design work, assigned to one designer (ticket had no further detail).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

items.s: [Open API V2] New endpoint for "sponsor" analytics for accounts
items.w: A new public API endpoint now exposes sponsor interaction analytics, views, clicks, favourites, meetings and messages, previously invisible.
items.y: Investigation confirmed the gap was by-design rather than a bug, and the original author recommended a dedicated endpoint over overloading the existing contract; clients actively hitting the gap made it a priority.
items.o: New GET /api/v2/statistics/sponsorInteractions endpoint returning paginated, filterable sponsor interaction rows (account, action, object, time) sourced from the sponsor statistics store under its own contract.

items.s: Unify Switch styles in expo-react-components
items.w: Switch component styling is centralized into the shared component library, removing three duplicated copies across frontend repos.
items.y: Design-system consolidation to reduce duplicated UI code across the frontend estate.
items.o: Switch styles are centralized in `expo-react-components`, reused across repositories with default-prop overrides in admin-ui, and removed from the individual repos.

items.s: Remove seated meetings module
items.w: The deprecated 'Seated Meetings' feature has been removed from the Hosted Buyer module and Module Management, decluttering the organizer Admin Panel and preventing accidental use of a redundant tool.
items.y: Prioritised as platform hygiene to streamline the organizer experience and retire deprecated functionality before it caused confusion or misuse.
items.o: The Seated Meetings sub-item and its module toggles were removed, direct URLs now redirect or return an access-denied state, and other Hosted Buyer functions (Meeting Wizard, Buyer/Exhibitor lists) are unaffected; historical meeting data is retained.

items.s: [Statistics Reports] New SponsorAccountsInteractionsReport — paginated sponsor interaction rows from sponsor_statistics
items.w: A new sponsor-interactions report class extracts paginated sponsor engagement rows from the dedicated sponsor statistics store.
items.y: Foundational report layer required to expose sponsor analytics under the Organizer Analytics area, built in parallel with the public API endpoint that depends on its contract.
items.o: New SponsorAccountsInteractionsReport class (prepare/validate/prepareQuery/resolvePaginated) hardwired to the sponsor object type, registered in ReportsList, returning sponsor interaction rows with a defined input/output contract.

items.s: Independent OTP Authentication Configuration for Company and Individual Profiles in Events
items.w: OTP login can be switched on separately for individual profiles and company (exhibitor) profiles, via a single email-first login form.
items.y: Corporate email servers often block OTP emails, so exhibitors on company emails couldn't log in.
items.o: Attendees keep passwordless login while exhibitors can use a password; existing events keep OTP on for both.

items.s: [EP] [BE] MeetingExportTask runs one INSERT per row — batch the cron_buffer insert
items.w: A meeting-export job that wrote one database row at a time now batches inserts into a single query, cutting write load on large exports.
items.y: Behaviour-preserving performance fix identified and validated against the working tree; safe, low-risk correction.
items.o: The SQL accumulation now happens correctly across the whole loop before a single batched INSERT executes, reducing write count from N to 1 per export batch with identical resulting data.

items.s: add /create-fe-tech-debt skill to scaffold FE Tech Debt tickets from Claude Code
items.w: A new Claude Code skill scaffolds FE Tech Debt tickets with the correct fixed fields automatically, eliminating recurring manual-entry mistakes.
items.y: Internal tooling improvement to remove a recurring, error-prone manual process for the frontend team.
items.o: A `create-fe-tech-debt` Claude Code skill creates Tech Debt tickets via the Atlassian MCP with the correct team/label/RGT+O fields and structured description, always showing a preview before creation.

items.s: Clean up bitbucket-pipelines.yml — drop legacy branch pipelines, remove hardcoded Discord token, dedupe ECR/SSM steps
items.w: CI pipeline cleanup removes dead legacy branches and a leaked Discord token in clear text, while de-duplicating repeated build/deploy steps.
items.y: Security remediation (leaked token) combined with CI maintainability cleanup as the team fully moved to the next14 stack.
items.o: Legacy branch pipelines and SonarQube steps are removed, the leaked Discord token is deleted and rotated, and the duplicated ECR/SSM build-deploy logic is consolidated into shared YAML anchors.

items.s: Include Pavilions as a searchable category in AI Search
items.w: Attendees can now discover exhibition Pavilions through AI Search, indexed as a distinct entity showing their grouped child exhibitors.
items.y: Part of the Search & Discovery initiative and Search Anatomy epic to make every key entity type instantly discoverable via AI Search.
items.o: Pavilion records are indexed as a distinct entity type with parent-child awareness and relevance boosting, appearing in Top Results and a dedicated Pavilions section while leaving regular exhibitor search unchanged.

items.s: Include Community Groups as a searchable category in AI Search
items.w: Attendees can now find Community Groups through AI Search using both exact names and topic-based intent, opening a search-driven path to the platform's community-building features.
items.y: Part of the Search & Discovery initiative and Search Anatomy epic to make community groups discoverable and drive community engagement.
items.o: Community Group records (name and description) are indexed as a distinct entity with semantic/intent matching, relevance ranking, and a dedicated Groups section; topic-tag indexing and member-count ranking were descoped pending data-model changes.

items.s: Include On-Demand Sessions as a searchable category in AI Search
items.w: Attendees can now search the on-demand content library by title, speaker, or topic through AI Search, with speaker-aware matching.
items.y: Part of the Search & Discovery initiative and Search Anatomy epic to make on-demand content discoverable and maximise the value of the recorded library.
items.o: On-Demand Session records are indexed (title, description, speakers, topics) with speaker-aware matching, weighted relevance ranking, and a dedicated On-Demand section distinct from live sessions; live-session search is unaffected.

items.s: replace barrel imports with deep imports for MUI and expo-react-components
items.w: Barrel imports across ~2,600 files are converted to deep imports and guarded by a lint rule, improving bundle size and dev build speed.
items.y: Performance and consistency cleanup, porting an already-documented convention from portal-ui into admin-ui.
items.o: Barrel imports are codemod-converted to deep imports, a `no-restricted-imports` ESLint rule is added to prevent regressions, and the convention doc is ported into admin-ui.

items.s: Android: Update app build sign process
items.w: Android's app-signing process is audited and standardized so release builds stay consistent and secure without exposed credentials.
items.y: Tech debt cleanup to reduce risk of signing failures and secret exposure in CI.
items.o: Signing configuration is audited, Gradle/CI updated to read credentials from secure storage, signed APK/AAB generation validated in CI, and troubleshooting steps documented for developers.

items.s: Remove SonarQube from frontend projects (next14, admin-ui, expo-react-components)
items.w: SonarQube analysis, unused and unreviewed, is removed from three frontend repos, cutting CI cost and dead configuration.
items.y: Low-risk cleanup to cut CI cost and remove unused tooling with no functional coupling to tests or builds.
items.o: `sonar-project.properties`, pipeline steps, and related config/doc references are removed from next14, admin-ui and expo-react-components; associated Bitbucket variables and server projects are slated for decommission.

items.s: Android: refactor handle push-notification
items.w: Android push-notification handling code was refactored; the ticket gives no further detail on the specific problem or outcome.
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
items.o: Push-notification handling code on Android was refactored; no further detail is documented on this ticket.

items.s: Ability to upload the SVG files
items.w: Lets organisers upload SVG files in the Website Builder so logos and icons render crisply at any resolution with smaller files.
items.y: Requested by IMEX; scalable graphics improve visual quality and page load performance.
items.o: SVGs are accepted, stored and listed alongside other images, render correctly on the event website, and malformed SVGs are rejected with an error.

items.s: Ability to edit the tracking links
items.w: Organizers can now edit the name and destination URL of existing Marketing Tracking Links in place, without recreating and re-distributing them.
items.y: Prioritised as a marketing-workflow quality-of-life fix so campaign links stay accurate without costly recreation and re-referencing.
items.o: An Edit action on each Tracking Link lets organizers update the name and landing page URL with validation, while the external tracked/short URL stays unchanged so existing campaign references keep working.

items.s: fix default typography for builder
items.w: The page Builder now uses current typography from the shared component library, fixing a visual mismatch with an outdated source.
items.y: Bug fix to bring the Builder's visual output in line with the current design system.
items.o: The Builder now sources its typography from `expo-react-component` instead of the old, outdated source.

items.s: [Android][Floor Plan] Offline ExpoFP archive integrity check compares MD5(file) to S3 ETag — offline floor plan never loads
items.w: A hash-comparison bug that silently deleted every offline floor plan download is fixed, so offline floor plans actually load for attendees.
items.y: Root-caused during regression testing of an unrelated SDK bump; confirmed as a pre-existing defect in ExpoPlatform's own offline wrapper, not the SDK.
items.o: The integrity check is fixed to treat `fileHash` as an ETag (skipping/adapting strict MD5 comparison for multipart or malformed values), the primary-download gate is fixed so a clean install still triggers the first download, and failures no longer report false success.

items.s: Add lightweight server-side t() translation helper for Server Components
items.w: Adds a server-side t() translation helper so Server Components can resolve i18n keys directly, removing the temporary NoAccessTranslated client wrapper.
items.y: Frontend tech debt: every future Server Component needing a translated string would otherwise need a client wrapper or ship raw English.
items.o: A memoised getServerTranslation(locale) helper is planned, with NoAccessTranslated removed and the 8 affected pages using the server t(), with no visual change.

items.s: Enable all conference flagged Floor Plan Location Selection for Exhibitor Events Beyond Assigned Booth
items.w: An opt-in setting lets Exhibitor Events map to any live Floor Plan location, not just the exhibitor's booth, closing a gap flagged in a feature-intake request.
items.y: A Feature Intake request (REQ-2026-060) flagged that a near-ready solution already existed and just needed a formal opt-in setting, low incremental engineering effort for real customer value.
items.o: A new admin checkbox lets Exhibitor Events select any live Floor Plan location (grouped as Your Stands / Floor Plan Locations / Predefined / free-text), with deduplication, while defaulting to today's booth-only behaviour when disabled.

items.s: Default View Setting (List / Grid / Calendar) for Sessions & Exhibitor Events
items.w: Organizers can now set List, Grid, or Calendar as the default Sessions page view, without engineering involvement, for content-dense schedules.
items.y: Discovery-stage enhancement tied to the broader Session Calendar View epic, giving organizers self-service control over content-dense schedules.
items.o: A "Default view" setting (List/Grid/Calendar) in Sessions Config controls the first-visit layout for the Sessions page; once an attendee manually toggles view, their choice persists locally, and Exhibitor Events included in Sessions inherit the same setting.

items.s: Embedded Analytics — TAM feedback & improvement requests (June 2026)
items.w: TAM-sourced feedback on the Embedded Analytics dashboards was consolidated into prioritised fixes: better date-range defaults, decluttering, filter totals.
items.y: Consolidates real TAM and client feedback (June 2026) to prioritise dashboard improvements against actual client usage pain within the New Analytics initiative.
items.o: A documented, prioritised set of improvement requests fed into the dashboard components — date-range defaults, decluttering, 2-decimal percentages, filter totals, Sessions simplification, Android/iOS login split, clearer labels, and new Meetings/Messages sections — with noted product-alignment items such as the date-r…

items.s: Analysis of the tools and approaches DS team can use to implement
items.w: A Data Science analysis of tools and approaches for AI Agenda Builder implementation, with no further detail documented on the ticket.
items.y: Tied to the AI Agenda Builder epic, but no further rationale is documented on this ticket.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

items.s: Bypass Payment Step When Basket Total Is £0 in Booking/Category Upgrade Flow
items.w: Attendees whose basket total drops to £0 in the booking or category upgrade flow can complete the booking without being asked for payment or billing details.
items.y: Asking for payment details on a free transaction is confusing friction for attendees and inconsistent with free registrations elsewhere.
items.o: A "Complete Booking" button replaces "Pay £0.00", the payment form is bypassed and a £0 invoice is sent only if the event's zero-price invoice setting is on.

items.s: Kiosk Badge Export
items.w: Organisers can export Kiosk badge printing data for attendees and exhibitor team members to Excel, showing unique and total prints per person.
items.y: Organisers need print data to track stationery usage and onsite activity during and after the live event.
items.o: A new "Kiosk" option under Data > Import/Export > Export produces a date-filtered .xlsx with per-person print counts and a timestamp per print.

items.s: Return back removed global setting for AI notetaker
items.w: The global AI Notetaker setting is restored in the App Builder, giving organizers back the centralized control the app team relies on.
items.y: Platform-health fix to restore a vital configuration removed in error.
items.o: The global AI Notetaker setting is back in the App Builder.

items.s: LexChat: self-host lexchat.js instead of loading from external siteURL
items.w: Serves the LexChat chatbot script from the platform's own origin instead of loading it at runtime from the legacy external siteURL bundle.
items.y: Frontend tech debt and reliability: remove an unpinned runtime dependency on an external host and simplify CSP.
items.o: lexchat.js is to be vendored and served under the /newfront base path, with the Script src no longer interpolating siteURL and the chatbot initialising unchanged.

items.s: Whitelist Trusted Embed Domains for Authenticated Iframe Content
items.w: Organizers can now whitelist trusted external domains so authenticated content, like On-Demand Sessions, plays correctly when embedded on partner sites.
items.y: Prioritised to unblock a broken cross-site embedding experience and enable partner distribution of authenticated content by letting organizers whitelist trusted origins for adjusted cookie headers.
items.o: A new 'Security settings / Trusted embed domains' section in Event Setup lets organizers add and remove whitelisted domains; for those origins the auth cookie is issued SameSite=None; Secure so embedded authenticated Sessions play seamlessly.
cus: Dubai World Trade Centre DWTC/ DXB Live

items.s: [Tech Debt][Android] GDPR/excluded (scanned) bypass applied inconsistently in Exhibitor profile meeting gate
items.w: Makes the Android exhibitor profile apply the same GDPR scanned-contact bypass as the personal profile, so the Meet button no longer disappears for scanned team members.
items.y: The two profiles contradicted each other, blocking legitimate meeting requests and confusing users.
items.o: The exhibitor profile meeting gate is to include the scanned/excluded status, so Meet availability matches the personal profile.

items.s: Unify Radio styles
items.w: Radio button styling is centralized into the shared component library, following the same consolidation already done for Switches.
items.y: Continuation of the design-system consolidation effort for shared form controls.
items.o: Radio styles are centralized in `expo-react-components`, reused across repositories with default-prop overrides in admin-ui, and removed from the individual repos.

items.s: support `q` search param on initial page load for news, participants, and sessions
items.w: A search term in a shared or global-search URL now correctly filters News, Participants and Sessions results, closing a known Global Search v2 gap.
items.y: Closes a documented, known limitation left behind by Global Search v2 (EP-44808), which visibly degrades the search experience today.
items.o: News, Participants and Sessions now read `q` from the URL on load and filter accordingly; the search input correctly displays the pre-applied term on all four pages; global-search "view all" links now carry the term through.

items.s: [TechDept] Research and fix admin permission-zone security issues (BAC, CSRF, XSS)
items.w: Re-verifies the 2018 security notes on admin permission zones against today's code and plans or makes fixes for confirmed access-control, CSRF and XSS issues.
