items.y: Security risk reduction: confirmed access-control and CSRF weaknesses in the admin panel need to be fixed or tracked.
items.o: Each tagged zone is to be marked still-real or already-fixed, with similar issues grouped and fixes made or split into assigned sub-tasks.

items.s: Translation: please apply the missing system translations.
items.w: Applies missing and corrected system translations, chiefly German, across exhibitor profile, registration photo, product list and notification screens.
items.y: Correct localisation for German-speaking events such as Hamburg Messe and Frankfurter Buchmesse tenants.
items.o: The listed EN/DE strings were decomposed into child tickets and corrected; the story is in testing.

items.s: [TechDept] [Cloning] Implement clone removal via the atom ledger
items.w: The admin "Remove clone" action now actually reverses a failed event clone's images, database rows and ledger entries, instead of doing nothing.
items.y: Needed so failed clones can actually be cleaned up rather than leaving orphaned images, rows and ledger entries behind.
items.o: `ExhibitionsController::removeAction` now deletes the cloned S3 images and Images rows per the copy ledger, deletes the cloned event (cascading DB cleanup plus the few non-cascading tables), and removes the clone job/step/progress bookkeeping.

items.s: Resolve circular dependencies in portal-ui module graph (60 cycles)
items.w: Breaks the 60 circular dependencies in the portal-ui module graph and adds a CI check so new cycles cannot creep back in.
items.y: Frontend tech debt: cycles defeat tree-shaking, slow hot reload and cause load-order bugs.
items.o: Store barrel imports are to be replaced by direct slice imports, type-only cycles converted to import type, and a madge --circular CI check with a shrinking allowlist added.

items.s: RFC-0008: DS ↔ Visitors integration contract for AI Agenda Builder
items.w: An RFC defines the DS-to-Visitors API contract for AI Agenda Builder recommendations so both teams can build in parallel instead of blocking on each other.
items.y: Cross-team alignment need identified in a DS-Visitors scoping call for the AI Agenda Builder epic (EP-50608), following the company's standard RFC process for multi-team initiatives.
items.o: A draft RFC document defines the request contract (user, booked slots, time window) and response contract (ranked session/event recommendations) between DS and Visitors, lists open questions and stakeholders, and is set up for the standard review process.

items.s: Analyze category data completeness across tenants (exhibitors/sessions vs. registered visitors)
items.w: A tenant-by-tenant audit of category-data completeness gives a go/no-go signal on whether AI Agenda Builder's matching logic has enough signal to work.
items.y: A data-quality audit is needed before committing to a recommendation design, since poor category coverage would starve the matching algorithm regardless of its quality.
items.o: A tenant-by-tenant completeness audit of category assignment on exhibitors/sessions and registered visitors, checking taxonomy consistency, delivered as a short summary with a go/no-go recommendation for AI Agenda Builder feasibility.

items.s: [iOS] Refactor project into multi-module SPM packages
items.w: Refactors the iOS app project into multi-module Swift Package Manager packages (ticket has no further detail).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to split the iOS codebase into separate SPM modules.

items.s: wrong styling for LeadCustomModal.tsx
items.w: The exhibitor lead-questions modal's styling is corrected to match the approved Figma design after shipping visually inconsistent.
items.y: Visual bug fix to bring the component in line with the design spec.
items.o: The modal's styling is updated to match the provided Figma reference.

items.s: flaky unit tests from async React.lazy imports — add global synchronous lazy test stub
items.w: A global React.lazy test stub, ported from a proven next14 fix, eliminates flaky non-deterministic unit test failures in admin-ui.
items.y: Ports an already-proven fix (EP-54584) from next14 to admin-ui, to stop non-deterministic CI failures that erode trust in the test suite.
items.o: A global synchronous `React.lazy` stub in `setupTests.tsx` renders lazy children immediately, wrapper tests are migrated off `waitFor`/`findBy` workarounds, and the suite is verified stable across multiple consecutive runs.

items.s: CustomHeader search: show categories selector on mobile + static in-flow panel
items.w: Mobile header search gains the categories selector desktop already has, and the panel now pushes content down instead of overlaying it, per Figma.
items.y: Closes a feature-parity gap between mobile and desktop search, aligning with the approved Figma design.
items.o: `searchPages` and `currentLanguage` are threaded through to the mobile search component so the categories selector renders per Figma; the search panel is changed from an overlay to an in-flow layout on both breakpoints.

items.s: API V3 Logs Admin Panel - UI Enhancements: Top Menu Button & Advanced Search
items.w: Adds a top-menu shortcut to the API V3 Logs page and a stackable Advanced Search that filters logs by params, request body or response content.
items.y: Two improvements proposed on EP-50318 were not yet actioned; support staff need to find specific API calls quickly.
items.o: A top navigation button is planned for all backend users, plus AND-combined conditions with Contains / Does not contain / == / != operators over serialised JSON.

items.s: API V3 - [POST] /api/v3/products/{id}/images (Upload product image from a file or a URL)
items.w: A new Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators upload images to a global product, with a main-image flag and preserved image ordering.
items.y: Part of the API V3 migration and the new global-vs-event-scoped product architecture, where media handling was deliberately split into dedicated endpoints to complete the product module.
items.o: POST /api/v3/products/{productId}/uploadImage uploads PNG/JPEG images to a global product, using a main flag to replace or append, preserving image order, with standard validations and response envelope (in progress).

items.s: API V3 - [DELETE] /api/v3/products/{id}/images/{imageId} (Remove product image)
items.w: A new Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators remove an image from a global product, correctly nulling the main-image reference when needed.
items.y: Part of the API V3 migration and new global-product media architecture; the delete counterpart completes image lifecycle management.
items.o: DELETE /api/v3/products/{productId}/images/{imageId} removes an image — nulling the product's main-image id if it was the main image, else dropping it from the list — while preserving remaining order, with 404 validations and standard response envelope (in progress).

items.s: API V3 - [POST] /api/v3/products/{id}/video (Upload product video)
items.w: A new Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators upload a hosted video file to a global product, switching the product's video type to uploaded, as part of the v3 product media architecture.
items.y: Part of the API V3 migration and new global-product media architecture, where video and embed handling was split into dedicated endpoints.
items.o: POST /api/v3/products/{productId}/uploadVideo stores an uploaded video, sets the product's hosted video URL, and switches its video type to uploaded, with validations and standard response envelope (in progress).

items.s: API V3 - [DELETE] /api/v3/products/{id}/video (Remove product video)
items.w: A new Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators unset a global product's uploaded video, clearing the video URL and association as the counterpart to the video-upload endpoint.
items.y: Part of the API V3 migration and new global-product media architecture; the removal counterpart completes video management.
items.o: DELETE /api/v3/products/{productId}/removeVideo clears the product's video URL and uploaded-video association, with 404 validation and standard response envelope; the post-unset video-type behaviour remains an open item pending core PATCH alignment (in progress).

items.s: Spike: Incorporate user interaction signals (likes/dislikes) into Recommender for AI Agenda Builder
items.w: Spike scoping whether AI Agenda Builder could use session likes/dislikes for smarter recommendations, without touching the live category-based Recommender rollout.
items.y: Flagged as an open gap during the DS review of AI Agenda Builder requirements; deliberately scoped as its own spike under Agenda Builder rather than the separate company-wide Recommender rollout epic, to avoid putting that stable rollout at risk.
items.o: Analysis-only deliverable: an inventory of where interaction data lives today, a recommended ingestion path into DS datasets with trade-offs, 1-2 candidate scoring approaches with effort estimates, and an explicit recommendation on next steps (new epic vs backlog addition vs defer). No code shipped.

items.s: [Tech] Create Media Module
items.w: Establishes the Products API media module in Public API v3 — the container for global-product image and video management endpoints — as part of the v3 endpoint migration.
items.y: Part of the API V3 migration and new global-product architecture, grouping the dedicated media endpoints into a coherent module.
items.o: The Products API media module scaffolding that groups the dedicated image and video upload/removal endpoints (in progress; the ticket body is a placeholder, so scope is inferred from the epic and sibling endpoints).

items.s: [TechDept] [EP] IDOR in ProfileController::signDocumentAction — buyer can sign/download any document via web endpoint
items.w: Closes an IDOR in the hosted buyer Sign button endpoint so a buyer can no longer sign or download documents belonging to other categories or events.
items.y: Security: a major broken object-level authorisation flaw (CWE-639) on the endpoint the production web UI uses.
items.o: The endpoint is to get an allow-list check, an event-scope check and an isBuyer() role guard, mirroring the EP-55044 fix.

items.s: [TechDept] [EP] IDOR in UploadController — docid POST param attaches uploaded file to any HostedBuyerBuyersDocuments
items.w: Closes an IDOR in the hosted buyer upload endpoint so uploaded files can only be attached to documents in the buyer's own category and event.
items.y: Security: the flaw broke the organiser's document-approval process and skewed hosted buyer document statistics.
items.o: The endpoint is to validate docid with the category allow-list and event-scope repository check, following the EP-55044 pattern.

items.s: Story 30. Enable New UI Registration Toggle
items.w: New "Use New UI Registration" toggle lets organizers migrate each event from legacy to new registration on their own schedule, defaulting off to protect existing events.
items.y: Follows the same proven kill-switch pattern already used for the New Website Builder and New UI Settings, and is required as the gating mechanism before the other 29 New UI Registration stories can be rolled out safely.
items.o: A new "Use New UI Registration" toggle in Event Setup > General > Settings, defaulting OFF; frontend registration routing and admin menu visibility switch between legacy and new flows based on the toggle, with the setting change taking effect immediately.

items.s: Integrations page - Back-end work
items.w: A new backend endpoint powers the Admin Panel Integrations page with a single catalog of every integration, tagged by category with per-event status.
items.y: Supports the new Admin Panel Integrations page — a consolidated, discoverable integrations catalog backed by a maintainable in-code registry.
items.o: GET /api/v1/integrations returns the full integrations catalog (hub + legacy) with names, descriptions, category tags, icons, and a per-event derived active flag; the catalog is maintained in code with a Confluence registry mirror and responses cached 10 minutes per event and language.

items.s: Exhibitor events fixes
items.w: Fixes two exhibitor-events display bugs: an empty floor-plan-location label and an incorrect Event Overlap flag on on-demand sessions.
items.y: Reported display/data-correctness defects with no linked epic; fixed as routine bug cleanup.
items.o: The empty floor plan location label is removed, and the Event Overlap indicator no longer shows for on-demand sessions.

items.s: Spike: extend existing Lambda to dual-write data into new pipeline's Kinesis (Data Protocol 2.0) for testing
items.w: Spike proposing a dual-write from the existing event pipeline into the new Data Protocol 2.0 Kinesis stream, to validate it with real traffic before frontend integration.
items.y: Needed to de-risk the new pipeline by testing it against representative production data server-side, in parallel with (not blocked by) the frontend experiment.
items.o: A design note, recommendation and effort estimate for extending the existing WS-pipeline Lambda to also copy each event into the new pipeline's Kinesis stream, covering schema mapping, record tagging to avoid double-counting, error isolation, and a kill switch.

items.s: Address Informa Analytics Display Feedback #2 (graph-level fixes & additions)
items.w: A second round of Informa-requested analytics fixes sharpens the reporting dashboards organizers use to prove event value.
items.y: Client Commitment to a flagship organizer's reporting needs.
items.o: Graph-level fixes and additions across the analytics display (exhibitor, attendee, app/platform).

items.s: Global Search. Quick links, Show all, and Back navigation
items.w: Quick links and Show all buttons on the Global Search page open a category listing with the query applied, with a Back button to return.
items.y: So users can jump into one category and get back to their search results easily.
items.o: Users move between the unified results and filtered listings without losing their search.

items.s: N+1 в InteractionScoresService::initForEvents при глобальном включении interaction scores (все ивенты тенанта)
items.w: Batches the interaction scores initialisation so enabling interaction scores globally no longer fires about three database queries per event across the tenant.
items.y: Performance: found in automated code review of EP-46974; large production tenants have hundreds or thousands of events.
items.o: Data is to be collected before the loop with one DISTINCT query, a single settings lookup and one chunked insertBatch after the loop.

items.s: [BE] ExhibitorEffectiveSettings: query LC-Pro orders as a fallback (settings-first) on the hot scan path
items.w: Reorders the exhibitor LC-Pro settings checks so purchase orders are only queried when the category or exhibitor setting is off, cutting database load on the scan path.
items.y: Performance follow-up raised in review of PR #4443 (EP-50210), whose own direction asked for purchase lookup as the fallback.
items.o: All LC-Pro getters are to evaluate settings first with purchase as fallback, with no behaviour change, after measuring the cost; close as won't-do if negligible.

items.s: Adding tracking for sponsor and sponsored product clicks
items.w: Adds view and click tracking for the Sponsored Exhibitors and Sponsored Products sliders in the mobile app, so app activity counts in sponsor statistics.
items.y: Sponsor performance was undercounted for events with heavy app usage, weakening the case for sponsorship sales.
items.o: iOS and Android are to record slider views and clicks by the documented rules and feed the same statistics pipeline as web sponsored cards.

items.s: Review the API SLOs
items.w: Reviews degraded Exhibitor Marketplace API endpoints against the new SLO framework and produces an improvement summary for the worst-performing latency sub-group.
items.y: The Exhibitor team just established a formal SLO/criticality framework and needed an initial review to identify the biggest reliability offenders before treating the targets as final.
items.o: Identified the degraded G_1200 API sub-group and its endpoint list within the Critical Exhibitor Marketplace component, and produced an analysis/summary of the problem for improvement planning (the underlying SLO page itself notes several figures still need 4xx/background-job noise filtered out before being treated as confirmed breaches).

items.s: Exception Handler Implementation
items.w: Builds a serverless exceptions handler (SQS, Lambda, DynamoDB) with Grafana boards for all exceptions and bug candidates, plus a dry-run ledger of the Jira tickets it would raise.
items.y: Internal observability: the MVP proves grouping yields one ticket per bug before the system is allowed to create Jira tickets.
items.o: A spec sized from a 38-day sample of the live stream and a repo exist; the MVP delivers two Grafana boards and a dry-run ticket ledger, now in review.

items.s: Skip the payment form when the basket total is 0 (100% discount) in the Booking flow
items.w: Free (100%-discount) bookings now complete in one step, skipping a redundant payment form for a frictionless checkout.
items.y: Customer-driven UX fix to remove friction from free bookings while keeping payments secure.
items.o: When the total is 0 the booking completes directly to the success page; the payment form is skipped with server-side price re-checks.

items.s: Translation Manager - Restrict English translation edits to authorised users
items.w: Restricts editing of English global translations in Translation Manager to specifically authorised users via a new EN-only permission.
items.y: Requested by Ajay Singh so that only four people can change English translations at global level.
items.o: Discovery defined a translations.update_en permission with service-layer locale guards, EN-only import gating and frontend hiding; open scope questions await confirmation.

items.s: Unify Checkbox styles
items.w: Rebuilds the shared Checkbox as a pure-CSS, SSR-safe theme control (mirroring Radio) to fix a glyph-clipping bug and end per-app checkbox styling duplication.
items.y: Direct precedent from the identical fix already applied to Radio (EP-55105); needed as the foundation phase before cross-repo checkbox unification can follow.
items.o: A new CSS-drawn MuiCheckbox theme override ships in expo-react-components (SSR-safe, no SVG, no clipping), the old bespoke Checkbox wrapper is removed, and two accent variants (primary/info) are exposed; cross-repo adoption in admin-ui/portal-ui is scoped as follow-up work.

items.s: Apply New Product Module on Frontend
items.w: Moves the frontend Products area onto the new DDD/CQRS Product module and v3 API introduced in EP-53873.
items.y: Platform modernisation: align products with the new modular architecture and unified error taxonomy.
items.o: The frontend is to use existing or new v3 Product endpoints following CQRS, with errors mapped to the shared taxonomy, tests and OpenAPI docs.

items.s: Unit tests fail on Node 22.4+/26: built-in Web Storage shadows jsdom localStorage
items.w: Fixes a Node 22.4+ regression where the built-in localStorage shadowed jsdom's, which had broken 10 unit tests and masked real regressions.
items.y: Environment regression from a Node upgrade; needed to keep the CI/dev test baseline trustworthy.
items.o: setupTests.js now forces jsdom's Storage implementation onto globalThis after initialization, restoring a fully green test suite and removing the noisy ExperimentalWarning.

items.s: Participant Management: Separate Category and Role Columns
items.w: Organisers see Category and Role as separate, independently filterable columns in Participant Management.
items.y: Cleaner participant segmentation and reporting for organisers before, during and after events.
items.o: Participant Management is to show distinct Category and Role columns with separate filters and sorting.

items.s: [SEO/GA4] Semantic H1 Tags for System Pages
items.w: Gives every listing and detail system page a single semantic H1 and passes page headings to the dataLayer, improving SEO and GA4 tracking.
items.y: SEO ranking for events such as Frankfurter Buchmesse and complete GA4 analytics for organisers.
items.o: Each system page is to render one correct H1 mapped to the analytics payload, including session names on session detail pages.

items.s: Build support for new OTP settings
items.w: Updates mobile login to read independent OTP toggles for Individual vs Company profiles so authentication stays correct once web ships the split settings.
items.y: Required to keep the mobile app in sync with the web/admin OTP toggle split so login behaves correctly per profile type.
items.o: Mobile app now reads two independent OTP flags, shows the OTP screen or username/password screen based on the profile type being authenticated (Attendee vs Exhibitor Company, with team members following the individual setting), and preserves current behavior for events still on the legacy single-toggle config.

items.s: Speed Networking: Claude skill to query per-participant exclusion data for missed-pair investigation
items.w: A new Claude-based tool lets the team query Speed Networking exclusion data in plain language, answering missed-pair questions without manual digging.
items.y: AI-readiness and efficiency: turn stored matching analytics into an ask-anything tool.
items.o: A Claude skill queries per-participant, per-slot exclusion data (from EP-54401) to answer ad-hoc missed-pair questions.

items.s: [TechDept] Refactor exhibitor-events selectors: dedupe SponsorsAutocomplete & SelectItem, use shared chip components
items.w: Dedupes duplicated exhibitor-events selector logic and swaps hand-rolled chips for the shared design-system chip components.
items.y: Cleanup surfaced from IMP-310 work to reduce duplication and drift between two near-identical components.
items.o: Shared search/render logic extracted into one component/hook, with chips now rendered via the expo-react-components shared chip/tag components.

items.s: Native Integration - Cvent (Event Management) — Phase 1: Inbound
items.w: Adds a native inbound Cvent integration to the Integration Hub, syncing attendees and exhibitors into ExpoPlatform with delta polling and a custom-questions import helper.
items.y: Integration Hub expansion: native connectors to major event platforms make ExpoPlatform easier to adopt alongside existing client tooling.
items.o: A polled OAuth2 Cvent → EP sync on the AutoUpdate engine is specified, matched on External ID, with a helper to pre-fill registration sections from Cvent question definitions; push-back is Phase 2.

items.s: Native Integration - Eventbrite — Phase 1: Inbound
items.w: Adds a native inbound Eventbrite integration to the Integration Hub, importing Eventbrite attendees as visitors with delta sync.
items.y: Integration Hub expansion to reduce manual data transfer for clients using Eventbrite.
items.o: A polled Eventbrite → EP visitor sync is specified, using a private OAuth2 bearer token, changed_since delta filtering and External ID matching; exhibitors are out of scope as Eventbrite has none.

items.s: Introduce mandatory field mapping in data import
items.w: Data import now blocks confirmation until each block's mandatory system fields are mapped, flagging the missing fields in the mapping popup.
items.y: Data quality: prevent bad imports at the point of mapping rather than cleaning up afterwards.
items.o: Per-block mandatory fields (e.g. First Name, Last Name, Email for participants) are defined; Confirm stays disabled and unmapped fields are named until all are mapped.

items.s: Bitbucket PR review workflow for Claude Code (bbpr CLI + skill + guide)
items.w: Ships a bbpr CLI and Claude Code skill so the frontend team can review Bitbucket PRs (list, diff, comment, approve) without leaving Claude Code.
items.y: Speeds up review turnaround for the FE team without waiting on an org-admin-gated official integration.
items.o: A bbpr CLI wrapper over the Bitbucket Cloud REST API, a bitbucket-pr-review Claude Code skill, a Bash permission allowlist, and a Confluence team setup guide, enabling list/diff/comment/approve on PRs from Claude Code.

items.s: Implement Microsoft Clarity in Admin Panel
items.w: Adds Microsoft Clarity session recordings and heatmaps to the Admin Panel so Product can see how organiser clients actually use key workflows.
items.y: A low-compliance-overhead first phase of EP-51003 analytics, shipped ahead of the slower GA4 legal review.
items.o: Clarity is to be deployed with masking on, separate staging and production projects and consent handling, gated on Legal updating the sub-processor list.

items.s: Custom colors for tracks
items.w: Tracks can use any custom colour through a full colour picker with hex input, alongside the existing 24 presets.
items.y: The fixed 24-colour palette stopped organisers from matching the event's brand exactly.
items.o: Track colours match the brand on session and exhibitor event cards, web and app, with readable text colour set automatically.

items.s: Native Integration - HubSpot (CRM) — Phase 1: Inbound
items.w: Ships a new inbound HubSpot integration (contacts/companies to visitors/exhibitors) with configurable event scoping, opening the platform to HubSpot-using organizers.
items.y: Expands the Integration Hub's native-integration catalogue to a widely used CRM platform, and lays the inbound foundation for the higher-value Phase 2 push-back capability.
items.o: A polled, delta-driven sync (Contacts to Visitors, Companies to Exhibitors) via the AutoUpdate engine, three configurable Event Scoping strategies (Association/List/Filter-based), full field mapping, identity matching, custom field/category mapping, and archival/deletion handling.

items.s: Native Integration - Salesforce (CRM) — Phase 1: Inbound
items.w: Adds a native inbound Salesforce integration to the Integration Hub, syncing Contacts or Leads as visitors and Accounts as exhibitors.
items.y: Integration Hub expansion: CRM connectors reduce manual data handling and support client adoption.
items.o: A polled Salesforce → EP sync via SOQL on SystemModStamp is specified, with Connected App OAuth, External ID matching and daily API-limit awareness; push-back is Phase 2.

items.s: Native Integration - Cvent (Event Management) — Phase 2: Push-Back
items.w: Adds Phase 2 push-back for the Cvent integration, writing ExpoPlatform visitor and exhibitor updates, including profile pictures and logos, back to Cvent.
items.y: Two-way sync keeps client systems of record current without manual re-entry.
items.o: Independently toggleable visitor, exhibitor and image push-back subscriptions are specified, reusing Phase 1 auth and ID mapping, with image-loop prevention flagged as a risk.

items.s: Native Integration - HubSpot (CRM) — Phase 2: Push-Back
items.w: Adds Phase 2 push-back for the HubSpot integration, writing ExpoPlatform visitor and exhibitor updates back to HubSpot Contacts and Companies.
items.y: Two-way CRM sync keeps client data consistent across systems.
items.o: Toggleable push-back subscriptions with a dedicated outbound field mapping are specified, needing extra write scopes; image push-back is not possible on HubSpot.

items.s: Native Integration - Salesforce (CRM) — Phase 2: Push-Back
items.w: Adds Phase 2 push-back for the Salesforce integration, writing ExpoPlatform visitor and exhibitor updates back to Salesforce Contacts, Leads and Accounts.
items.y: Two-way CRM sync for clients whose system of record is Salesforce.
items.o: Toggleable push-back with its own outbound mapping is specified, sharing Phase 1 credentials and the daily API quota; image push-back is not applicable.

items.s: Unify favouriting into FavouriteService with per-object-type handlers
items.w: Consolidates all favouriting into one FavouriteService with per-object-type handlers instead of controller switch statements.
items.y: Follow-up from the EP-53978 / PR #4431 review to reduce duplication and keep new favouriting logic in one place.
items.o: A single service with visitor, exhibitor, product, brand and session handlers is planned, with public writes migrating gradually and reads optionally consolidated.

items.s: Bulk connection delete is not private-favourite-aware
items.w: Bulk connection delete now also removes opted-out users' private favourites, so they can bulk-remove what they bulk-added.
items.y: Found in QA scope inventory of the EP-53978 private favourites work; the asymmetry broke the mobile bulk-remove flow.
items.o: Bulk delete is aligned with single-disconnect behaviour and removes the owner's private favourite rows; the fix is in testing.

items.s: N+1 queries in V3 Sponsors list — exhibitor logo gate resolves per-sponsor at serialization
items.w: Removes an N+1 query pattern in the V3 Sponsors list, where each sponsor's exhibitor logo setting was resolved separately at serialisation.
items.y: Performance regression introduced by EP-47975's exhibitor logo gating on the sponsor chain.
items.o: Logo gating is to be resolved once per page rather than per sponsor, keeping the same image output.

items.s: [DS] Onboarding Spike: Round Tables codebase & architecture review
items.w: Onboarding spike that brings a second developer up to speed on the Round Tables architecture ahead of three upcoming feature stories.
items.y: Necessary knowledge-transfer step before HV-137/HV-143/HV-139 can safely begin implementation.
items.o: A written architecture alignment (current design summary in the new developer's own words, proposed extension points for each of the three stories, and agreed risks/open questions), reviewed by the original developer.

items.s: Enforce view-only / event scope for admin permissions (deny-by-default in AccessControl)
items.w: Makes admin permissions deny-by-default so an admin set to view-only or no access on one event no longer gets full access on every other event.
items.y: Security finding split out of the EP-55010 admin lockout investigation; restricted admins could act on events they should not.
items.o: The fix to fetchAccessZone is scoped with explicit caution, as a naive deny-by-default could lock out many production admins across tenants.

items.s: [BE] Global rate-limit for Utils::sendException with repeat counting
items.w: Adds a global rate limit with repeat counting to exception notifications, so an outage no longer floods the alert channel with identical messages.
items.y: Generalises the local AI-search rate limit from EP-47675 to the whole platform and removes that workaround.
items.o: A per-call-site signature with memcached marker and counter suppresses repeats for 300s, reports the repeat count next time and fails open if the cache is down.

items.s: API V3 - [POST] /api/v3/products/{id}/media (Upload product media file)
items.w: New Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators upload media files to a global product, completing the v3 product-media capability.
items.y: Closes a known gap in the ongoing Public API v3 endpoint migration, keeping the media capability consistent with the already-shipped image (EP-55240) and video (EP-55242) upload endpoints.
items.o: New POST /api/v3/products/{id}/media endpoint supporting up to 10 files per product, content-based format validation, a 5MB cap, PDF thumbnailing, and a standardized response envelope.

items.s: API V3 - [DELETE] /api/v3/products/{id}/media/{mediaId} (Remove product media file)
items.w: New Public API v3 endpoint removes a product media file safely, only physically deleting it once no other owner still references it.
items.y: Required counterpart operation to make the new product-media API usable end to end.
items.o: New DELETE /api/v3/products/{id}/media/{mediaId} endpoint unlinks a media file from a product; the underlying file/row is physically deleted only when no other owner (exhibitor, schedule, message, etc.) still references it.

items.s: [DS] Onboarding Spike: Data Protocol 2.0 pipeline scope & architecture review (Elmurod)
items.w: Onboarding spike bringing a new DS engineer up to speed on the Data Protocol 2.0 pipeline architecture before hardening and testing work begins.
items.y: Front-loads necessary context before the 10-item hardening roadmap (dead-letter store, reprocessing, ClickHouse migration tooling, Australia routing, observability, etc.) and in-flight dual-write tickets land.
items.o: A written summary of the pipeline architecture in the engineer's own words, reviewed by senior team members, plus documented open questions before the follow-on tickets start.

items.s: Add isScheduled:boolean to session items in sessionsCalendarView response
items.w: Adds an isScheduled flag to the session calendar API so the calendar UI can highlight sessions already in a user's personal agenda.
items.y: Direct frontend requirement to complete the calendar-view feature built under EP-54343.
items.o: Every session item in the day/week sessionsCalendarView response now carries an isScheduled boolean (always false for guests), with no other change to the response contract.

items.s: [EP:dev] N+1 + PHP-8 null-deref in hosted-buyer agent displayName lookups
items.w: Fixes an N+1 query and a null-dereference bug in hosted-buyer agent name lookups that would hard-fatal once the platform moves to PHP 8.
items.y: Flagged as a moderate-severity finding in an audit; must be fixed before the planned PHP 8.x migration to avoid a production outage.
items.o: Implementation hints proposed (batch-loading agent attributes once instead of per-agent, and null-guarding the read using the safe pattern already present elsewhere in the same controller); final implementation left to the developer.

items.s: [TechDept] [EP:dev] N+1 in participant export getParticipantData — per-event 'SELECT title' query per account (N×M events queries)
items.w: Removes an N+1 in participant export, where a separate event-title query ran for every account and every event it was active in.
items.y: Performance defect found in audit (moderate severity) on the export hot loop.
items.o: Event titles are to be loaded once and reused across the export, including the moderator all-events branch, with unchanged output.

items.s: Exhibitor Events Calendar View - Mobile
items.w: Adds a full calendar view (1-day/3-day grid, overlap handling, filters, search) to the mobile Exhibitor Events screen, matching the Sessions calendar experience.
items.y: Closes a feature gap versus the existing Sessions calendar view and the exhibitor-events-in-sessions-calendar work, neither of which touched the independent Exhibitor Events screen.
items.o: A full calendar view for Exhibitor Events on mobile: 1-day/3-day grid, week-glance strip, overlap handling with overflow bottom sheets, track quick-filters, in-calendar search, filters, a Today button, and a toggle back to List View, driven by a web-configured default-view setting.

items.s: reduce dev-mode compilation graph: lazy-load heavy layout subtrees and enable webpack lazyCompilation
items.w: Cuts portal-ui dev-mode page compile times by lazy-loading heavy layout subtrees and enabling webpack lazyCompilation.
items.y: Developer productivity: slow dev compiles waste engineering time on every page change.
items.o: Measured with lazyCompilation: profile 35s to 15.7s, news 20s to 10.6s, groups 21.5s to 3.7s, with per-page graphs down to 9.9k–12.3k modules.

items.s: Add relevant logs to data import
items.w: Each data import produces a result log, with a summary in Log Info and a downloadable per-row file showing what was created, updated or skipped and why.
items.y: Import transparency, so admins can trust and fix imports, especially where duplicates arise from fake email generation settings.
items.o: A summary with counts, status and fake-email state is logged, plus the uploaded file echoed back with Row, Action and Reason columns for re-upload.

items.s: File size upload issue on data import
items.w: Lets admins import one data file of any size and get one trustworthy result, instead of splitting large files by hand.
items.y: Data integrity during bulk onboarding ahead of events, when errors matter most.
items.o: Required behaviours are set: one upload is one job and re-running after an interruption never duplicates data; the processing design is left to the team.

items.s: [BE-NonTM]Translation: please apply the missing system translations.
items.w: Adds missing and corrected EN/DE notification translations for Frankfurter Buchmesse and DLG PotatoEurope exhibitors on live events.
items.y: Urgent client need: the events were live and exhibitors were already using the platform.
items.o: Approval and time-change notification strings are to be added and corrected in EN and DE.

items.s: Add MultiStandLocation component and migrate sponsors to ExhibitorCard
items.w: Adds a MultiStandLocation component so multi-stand exhibitors display readably, and merges Sponsors onto ExhibitorCard so sponsor listings show location, tags and products.
items.y: Needed to match the Figma design-system pattern (one stand plus a "+N" counter) and stop duplicating/drifting location-building logic across every consumer app.
items.o: New MultiStandLocation component ships in expo-react-components; ExhibitorCard now builds its own location from exhibitor.halls; ISponsor is merged into IExhibitor so SponsorsPopup renders full ExhibitorCards; the old SponsorCard is deprecated but not deleted, pending consumer migration.

items.s: Spike: EDA on historical user interaction data for Recommender scoring enhancement
items.w: EDA on historical like/favourite data to determine whether it's dense enough to build and evaluate a smarter, interaction-aware session recommender.
items.y: Needed hard evidence before committing engineering effort to either the category-weight or embedding-similarity scoring approach still on the table.
items.o: An EDA write-up covering historical interaction volume/density (an updated sparsity verdict versus the 2023 LightFM baseline), exposure-bias/impression-data findings, and a recommendation on offline vs. online evaluation strategy for the two remaining candidate approaches.

items.s: Move account creation earlier in Registration flow (prerequisite for cart approach) - ON HOLD
items.w: Creates the registrant's account before payment starts rather than after submission, as a prerequisite for the cart payment approach (on hold).
items.y: Blocks the cart/basket payment approach in EP-55566, which needs a reserved account before payment.
items.o: Draft criteria move account creation ahead of payment, update ordering tests and audit dependent code; the story is on hold.

items.s: Handle VAT charged when VAT-number check service is unavailable at checkout - ON HOLD
items.w: Defines how checkout should handle VAT when the VAT-number check service is down, instead of silently overcharging exempt business customers (on hold).
items.y: Invoice correctness and tax compliance; overcharged customers need formal invoice corrections.
items.o: Options to block checkout, charge and auto-correct with a refund and credit note, or retry are set out for a product and engineering decision; on hold.

items.s: Enhancing Exhibitor Import to Attach Brands Across Events
items.w: Exhibitor import and adding exhibitors from the global database now attach their existing brands, and brand–product links, to the new event.
items.y: Brands are long-term assets used in sponsorship and search, but exhibitors had to recreate them for every event edition.
items.o: Recurring events carry exhibitors' brands over automatically, with no new import column and no duplicate brands.

items.s: Region filters
items.w: An optional Regions subfilter under Country for exhibitor, product, brand, pavilion, delegate, speaker and buyer listings on web.
items.y: Some organisers collect region at registration and want visitors to narrow results within a country.
items.o: Visitors expand a country to pick regions, like category subfilters; it's off by default and web only.

items.s: [TechDept] [EP:dev] PaymentInvoiceService: tolerate null ambient lang when generating invoices (TypeError hardening)
items.w: Hardens invoice generation so a null ambient language no longer throws a TypeError that could return a 500 after a payment has already succeeded.
items.y: Tech debt agreed in the PR #4578 review: the hazard is real though rare, and would give clients a 500 for a recorded success.
items.o: Invoice generation is to tolerate a null language across the four no-language call sites, closing the TypeError path.

items.s: [Tech debt] - Chosen [Anchor option] is not updated after element [Anchor] rename
items.w: Keeps the chosen anchor option on linked buttons and links in sync when the anchor element is renamed in the site builder.
items.y: Frontend tech debt; stale anchor links break on-page navigation that organisers have set up.
items.o: Renaming an anchor is to update the anchor option selected on linked clickable elements.

items.s: Community-as-home-page redirect drops query params and URL fragment
items.w: Makes the community-as-home-page redirect keep query parameters, the URL fragment and the locale, so links such as /#signIn still work.
items.y: Frontend routing tech debt: deep links like the sign-in modal were silently broken on community-as-home sites.
items.o: The redirect target is to carry query, fragment and locale through, avoiding the lossy client-side hop.

items.s: Global search. UI improvements based on feedback from IMEX
items.w: Global Search results page refinements: a fixed search field under the banner, counts on Show all buttons, a bold results title, even News cards.
items.y: User feedback after the new search page launched asked for a more streamlined page.
items.o: The results page is cleaner, counts match their sections, and sponsored blocks are renamed Sponsored Exhibitors and Sponsored Products.

items.s: [BE] Onboarding into Ticketing functionality + study new code architecture (PR #4510) for future refactoring
items.w: Onboarding/research task building developer fluency in Ticketing and a proposed new architecture (PR #4510) ahead of a planned Ticketing refactor.
items.y: Prerequisite knowledge-building step for a planned future Ticketing refactor.
items.o: Developer understanding of Ticketing end-to-end and the new architecture pattern from PR #4510, plus a documented list of candidate refactor areas; no code changes.

items.s: IconModal: paddings and title typography do not match the Design System
items.w: Fixes IconModal's padding, gaps and title typography to match the Figma design system exactly, removing per-consumer style patches across ~41 call sites.
items.y: Design-system-fidelity issue surfaced by comparing the shipped component against its Figma spec node; the current "correct" spacing only worked by coincidence, not by design.
items.o: Reworked slot styles (uniform 24px padding, single 32px gap, correct 18px/1.2 bold title, 8px radius plus border, 424px default width), full Storybook coverage of slot combinations, and removal of local sx/width workarounds in admin-ui.

items.s: [TechDept] profile products: guard add/edit form against direct ?add URL access
items.w: Closes a bypass where direct URL navigation let restricted users open the add/edit product form even when the UI correctly hid the button.
items.y: Security/business-logic gap discovered in review; needed to prevent users from exceeding configured product limits or editing restrictions via URL manipulation.
items.o: Routing decisions now use the same single "can add/can edit" gate as the button; unauthorized direct navigation redirects to the product list instead of rendering the form, with backend enforcement also to be verified.

items.s: Migrate Statistic Events from WebSocket to HTTP ingest gateway
items.w: Moves browser statistic events off the shared WebSocket to the data science team's HTTP ingest gateway, which validates and forwards them to S3 and ClickHouse.
items.y: The data science team is replacing the path, taking our backend out of the analytics flow.
items.o: The three analytics WS actions (statistics, online dwell, notification clicks) are to post to the ingest gateway; chat, presence and push stay on WebSocket.

items.s: [Spike] Research the steps needed to change the search engine to AI Search
items.w: Scoping spike estimating the effort, risks and infrastructure needed to migrate the Exhibitors search engine to AI Search.
items.y: Needed so the team can estimate EP-55996 confidently and the EM can plan the work into a sprint.
items.o: A technical brief (target state, gap analysis, risks/open questions, phased plan with T-shirt estimates) published and linked to EP-55996.

items.s: [Invoice&Payments] Add Account ID / ID as a search parameter on Transaction Dashboard and Invoice Payments pages
items.w: Extends Transaction Dashboard and Invoice Payments search to match Account ID, so client ACI Asia-Pacific & Middle East can cross-check transactions against Stripe quickly.
items.y: Direct client request and follow-on from the earlier search feature (EP-54690), confirmed feasible by engineering.
items.o: The existing search field/button on both pages now also matches (partial) Account ID / ID, with the same trigger, reset and empty-state behavior as the original name/email search.

items.s: Enforce per-event access scope for configured admins (deny-by-default in AccessControl)
items.w: Admins restricted on one event stay restricted on every event they have not been explicitly granted, instead of falling back to the default access template.
items.y: Organisers expect per-event restrictions to hold; the bypass is a security and trust issue.
items.o: A new resolution order is defined: explicit row wins, any configured admin is denied elsewhere, and only never-configured admins use DEFAULT SETTINGS.

items.s: Post Code Field Validation for Registration Forms
items.w: Adds validation for the post code field on registration forms (details are in a linked Confluence page only).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to validate post codes entered in registration forms.

items.s: All 404s return HTTP 200 — soft-404 caused by the next-i18n-router rewrite
items.w: Makes non-existent pages return a real HTTP 404 instead of 200, fixing soft-404s caused by the next-i18n-router rewrite.
items.y: SEO and monitoring: junk paths were indexable and uptime checks could not tell broken routes from healthy ones.
items.o: The status loss is to be pinned down in the rewrite path and fixed so notFound() yields a 404 across the app, including site-builder slugs.

items.s: [Tech] Product uploads: move storage I/O out of the DB transaction; lock the product row against concurrent lost updates
items.w: Fixes product upload endpoints so slow file I/O no longer blocks the DB transaction and concurrent uploads can no longer silently overwrite each other's result.
items.y: Correctness and scalability defect discovered in the product upload path; needed before it causes data loss or connection exhaustion at scale.
items.o: Uploads now validate and store the file first with no open transaction, then link it in a short transaction with permission/limit checks re-run; failed links auto-clean the stored file; concurrent writes to the same product now queue via row locking instead of silently overwriting; ~30 new unit tests, API contract unchanged.

items.s: Cache-Control: public is applied to every route regardless of auth or cookies
items.w: Fixes a caching bug where cookie-dependent/signed-in pages were marked publicly cacheable, risking one visitor's personalized page being served to another.
items.y: DevOps enabled CDN caching for custom domains and asked the frontend team to confirm cookie-dependent pages weren't marked public before extending caching further.
items.o: Routes split into anonymous (kept public/cacheable) vs personal (private, no-store) groups; Vary: Cookie added where relevant; audited that no public response carries Set-Cookie; a route/header matrix handed to DevOps.

items.s: [TechDebt] Global Search: remaining backend refactoring from code review
items.w: Addresses remaining Global Search backend code-review findings: constructor-based config, policy-layer access checks, and hardened error handling.
items.y: Agreed follow-up from the EP-47675 Global Search code review.
items.o: Constructor-based configuration, access rule moved into a policy, hardened typing and exception handling, followed by a review/QA pass.

items.s: Utils::addToQueue reports its own SQS failure through itself — exponential retry loop that OOMs the process
items.w: Stops Utils::addToQueue reporting its own SQS failures through itself, which created a growing retry loop that ran the process out of memory.
items.y: A generic reliability defect found during testing of EP-53978; any SQS outage or credential issue could crash processes.
items.o: The failure path is to be decoupled from the queue it reports on, so an SQS failure is logged once rather than looping to OOM.

items.s: Re-check which interaction events reach ClickHouse for an opted-out actor, and decide per action
items.w: Audits which interaction events still reach ClickHouse for users who opted out of networking, and decides per action whether to suppress them.
items.y: Privacy and GDPR: decide the remaining ~40 action codes deliberately rather than defect by defect.
items.o: A per-action table over AnalyticsActionEnum is to record emit channel, whether it identifies the actor and the decision to keep or suppress.

items.s: [TechDept] [adminUI] Sentry: tag events with tenant and user identity
items.w: Tags adminUI Sentry events with tenant, event and user identity so errors can be found by customer.
items.y: Observability: support and engineering need to search errors by customer.
items.o: After auth, setUser plus ep.tenant and ep.event_id tags are to be set and cleared on logout, using indexed tags rather than contexts.

items.s: [portalUI] Sentry: tag events with tenant and user identity
items.w: Tags portalUI Sentry events with tenant, event and user identity so errors can be found by customer.
items.y: Observability, aligned with the adminUI sibling ticket so one search works across both projects.
items.o: After auth, setUser plus ep.tenant and ep.event_id tags are to be set and cleared on logout, using the same tag names as adminUI.

items.s: [TechDept] [adminUI] Sentry: upload source maps so production stack traces are readable
items.w: Uploads adminUI source maps to Sentry so production stack traces show real functions and lines instead of minified bundle positions.
items.y: Observability: readable traces are needed to diagnose production errors.
items.o: Hidden source maps are to be generated, uploaded via @sentry/vite-plugin with a secured CI token, deleted locally, and matched to the runtime release.

items.s: [portalUI] Sentry: confirm source map upload is not silently skipped in CI
items.w: Confirms portalUI source map uploads to Sentry actually run in CI rather than being silently skipped when the auth token is missing.
items.y: Observability: silently minified traces are only discovered when someone needs them.
items.o: The token is to be checked or added as a secured pipeline variable, with an option to fail the production build when it is missing.

items.s: [portalUI] Sentry: Report a problem action that flushes the replay buffer

items.s: [TechDept][CLONING-2][BE] Stage 1 — dependency direction and layer boundaries
items.w: Fixes the Cloning module's inverted dependencies so its core logic can be unit tested without a database and can't be silently broken by internal renames.

items.o: Contract DTOs introduced so Domain stops importing Contract; Application now depends only on ports; use-case classes moved into Application without dragging Infrastructure along; a thin CLI presentation layer added; the internal service-locator pattern removed; the contract split into read vs command halves, with deptrac reporting zero Domain/Application violations at completion.

items.s: [TechDept][CLONING-2][BE] Stage 2 — invert the legacy dependency

items.s: [TechDept][CLONING-2][BE] Document the SharedKernel / Platform / framework rules and fix the stale namespaces

items.s: flaky unit tests returned in CI — fix root cause and close the gap in the qa agent standards
