items.s: ExpoIntelligence — requirements analysis & data-presence audit
items.w: Audited data availability for all 22 planned ExpoIntelligence metrics so the exhibitor-insights dashboard can be scoped against what the platform can actually deliver.
items.y: Committed to on a 7 Aug team call as a prerequisite before any ExpoIntelligence story could be properly estimated or started.
items.o: A findings report classifying each of the 22 metrics as Have/Partial/Missing with rough effort signals, cross-checked against the DP2.0 Parity Matrix; no dashboards or queries were built, per the ticket's explicit scope.

items.s: US-1: Access via unique email link (v1)
items.w: Exhibitors can open the ExpoIntelligence insights portal from a tokenised email link without an ExpoPlatform login.
items.y: Foundation for the Exhibitor Insights Portal, delivered through email campaigns.
items.o: A token scoped to one exhibitor and event with expiry, revocation and read-only access is specified; delivery and revocation ownership are still undefined.

items.s: US-2: Solo exhibitor view
items.w: A solo exhibitor lands directly on their own guided journey and full insights report in the ExpoIntelligence portal.
items.y: Core use case of the Exhibitor Insights Portal.
items.o: All 7 sections are to populate from live data scoped to the exhibitor, with no stand switcher; sizing awaits metric definitions and spike EP-56324.

items.s: US-3: Stand summary (parent + children)
items.w: Parent exhibitors see a Stand Summary aggregating their own and all child exhibitors' KPIs in the insights portal.
items.y: Exhibitors with sub-exhibitors need a stand-level picture.
items.o: Summed and deduplicated KPIs with a combined benchmark are specified; blocked on the dedup rule for buyers who met several children.

items.s: US-4: Child switcher
items.w: Parent exhibitors can switch from the Stand Summary into any individual child exhibitor's insights report.
items.y: Part of the Exhibitor Insights Portal parent/child experience.
items.o: A switcher listing parent and children is specified, with one-click return and children unable to see siblings; depends on US-3.

items.s: US-5: White-label branding
items.w: The insights portal carries the event's own logo on the gate, report header and exports, falling back to the ExpoPlatform mark.
items.y: The portal should look like the organiser's product to its exhibitors.
items.o: The event logo is to be pulled from Admin → General → Logo via the Event API; flagged as the lowest-risk story for early pickup.

items.s: US-6: Guided journey + one-page report
items.w: Builds the insights portal's guided journey and one-page report, with 12 insight cards over 7 sections and Excel/PDF export.
items.y: Deliver parity with the approved ExpoIntelligence prototype.
items.o: Every number is to trace to a defined metric query and exports include all unlocked sections; blocked on ~40 metric definitions.

items.s: US-7: Benchmarks vs similar exhibitors
items.w: Shows exhibitors their percentile position against an anonymised peer cohort from the same event.
items.y: Benchmarks give exhibitors context for their event performance.
items.o: Cohorts of at least 8 with non-identifiable peers are specified; blocked on Legal anonymity sign-off and an undefined cohort definition.

items.s: US-8: Buyer interaction insights
items.w: Shows exhibitors which buyers viewed, favourited, searched, messaged or met them, with profile context.
items.y: Buyer insight is a core value of the Exhibitor Insights Portal.
items.o: Listing only interacting buyers within lead-sharing rules is specified; blocked on undefined lead-sharing rules and buyer interaction coverage gaps.

items.s: US-9: LLM coaching narrative
items.w: Adds an LLM coaching layer to the insights portal that writes plain-English narrative and a prioritised action plan per section, never inventing numbers.
items.y: Part of the ExpoIntelligence vision, but deliberately deferred until the dashboards are validated commercially.
items.o: Deterministic numbers with LLM-written narrative, cached per exhibitor and data version, are specified; low priority per the 7 Aug team decision.

items.s: US-10: Paywall on dashboard (nice-to-have)
items.w: Lets exhibitors self-purchase the full insights report from a paywalled preview on their dashboard (nice-to-have, v2).
items.y: A potential revenue stream for ExpoIntelligence, deferred behind v1 email-link access.
items.o: A locked preview, purchase unlock and auditable entitlement are specified; not to be sized until v1 ships and a payment decision lands.

items.s: Bulk respond: remove full-team prefetch and pre-Apply sweep in favor of a post-apply grid refetch
items.w: Removed a slow full-team prefetch that delayed opening Bulk Respond for large exhibitor teams, replacing it with an instant open and a simple post-apply data refresh.
items.y: The prefetch (and a second hidden sweep) existed only to support an optimistic client-side patch; removing them entirely, rather than swapping the data source, eliminated both the delay and a data-correctness risk in the patch logic.
items.o: Bulk Respond now opens instantly regardless of team size; after a successful bulk action, only the current grid page is refetched fresh from the backend and every other cached page is invalidated.

items.s: Media module: migrate Contract signatures from SharedKernel VOs to primitives
items.w: Migrated the Media module's public contract from internal value objects to plain primitives, keeping it aligned with the platform's modular, extraction-ready architecture.
items.y: New-monolith architecture convention adopted in EP-52842; the Media module predated it and needed to catch up, the same as Categories/Locations/Exhibition already had.
items.o: Media module Contract signatures now use primitives (int, int[], ?int); VO translation moved into facade implementations; consuming code (mainly the Product module) updated accordingly.

items.s: Add FBM Gabarito to remaining pages [Android]
items.w: Rolled out the FBM app's Gabarito typography to all remaining Android screens (~1010 elements across 451 layouts) for one consistent look end to end.
items.y: Client/brand-consistency requirement for the FBM app; a PO note flagging residual visual risk indicates this shipped ahead of an event under time pressure.
items.o: Gabarito Semibold/Light configured platform-wide for FBM in AppBuilder; ~252 components (AppCompatTextView, TextView, MaterialButton, chips, radio buttons, text inputs) migrated onto the dynamic-font path; verified with no truncation/overflow on a smoke-tested set of high-traffic screens.

items.s: Native Integration: Infosalon Exhibitor Push + SSO
items.w: Adds a native InfoSalons integration that pushes ExpoPlatform exhibitor data to the InfoSalons Exhibitor Portal and supports SSO login.
items.y: Extends the Integration Hub, following the Aditus exhibitor push pattern (EP-46657).
items.o: An ongoing outbound sync on create and update with API-key auth, plus JWT-signed SSO login and account sync endpoints, is specified.

items.s: Banner sizing: single source of truth instead of hand-maintained per-page aspect-ratio constants
items.w: Replacing four layers of hardcoded, drift-prone banner-size constants with the backend's own size data to stop paid sponsor banners from being repeatedly cropped in production.
items.y: Recurring, customer-reported production incidents on paid placements made the pattern of patching exceptions on top of exceptions unsustainable; root-causing was judged cheaper than the next incident.
items.o: A plan to drive banner aspect ratios from the API's own per-breakpoint size object (already returned by the backend but never read by the frontend), removing the per-page exception maps, aligning skeleton and resolved rendering, and replacing a silent 16:9 crop fallback with a dev-time failure.

items.s: Return Button to Global search result page
items.w: Added a "Back to search results" path so attendees can return to their exact Global Search context instead of redoing the search after opening a result.
items.y: Direct UX gap in the unified Global Search experience, part of the broader Search Anatomy initiative.
items.o: A "Back to search results" path now appears on detail pages reached via Global Search (restoring the query), consistently across all result types, and is absent when the detail page was reached any other way.

items.s: [TechDept][TM-dev/BE] Monolith: implement ICU MessageFormat rendering in the translation layer (plural/select)
items.w: Adds ICU MessageFormat rendering to the monolith's translation layer so plural and select translations display correctly instead of as raw ICU text.
items.y: The agreed follow-up to a risk explicitly accepted in EP-55658.
items.o: The monolith translation service is to render ICU plural, select and nested arguments from the Translation Manager's ICU form.

items.s: Reuse the unsaved changes guard on the rest of the iframe-embedded admin pages
items.w: Extends the unsaved-changes guard to the other iframe-embedded admin pages, so parent-frame navigation no longer silently drops edits.
items.y: The same data-loss bug EP-56400 fixed remained reproducible elsewhere in the admin.
items.o: The reusable guard is to be wired into the remaining embedded pages, replacing each page's own partial navigation warning.

items.s: Internal admin panel search
items.w: Adds a persistent Admin Panel search that finds pages, settings, entities and hidden text such as tooltips and dropdown options, and jumps straight to them.
items.y: Admins waste time hunting for settings; distinct from the customer-facing Global Search.
items.o: A header search bar is specified over an index of page titles, labels, help text, placeholders and option values, including Analytics & Reports.

items.s: Codeception: BaseCest leaks process-wide static state between tests (ExpoConfig::$values), manufacturing false failures in full-suite runs
items.w: Resets the ExpoConfig static cache between Codeception tests so full-suite runs stop producing false failures that look like product bugs.
items.y: Reliable tests: leaked static state manufactures failures unrelated to the code under test.
items.o: The second process-wide static is to be reset centrally after a verification run; the first leak was fixed in PR #4880.

items.s: Flaky unit test: PublicApiLogFiltersReaderTest fails on a warm cache — Cache::getCachedResult skips the mocked call
items.w: Fixes a flaky unit test for PublicApiLogFiltersReader that fails whenever the CloudWatch filters cache is already warm.
items.y: Deterministic cache-dependent failures undermine confidence in the test suite.
items.o: The test is to isolate or bypass the cache so its expectation holds regardless of cache state.

items.s: [BE Test fail] Import suites are red — 53 failures across api-admin and cli, and nothing anywhere turns red
items.w: Gets the red import test suites passing again: 53 failures across api-admin and cli that nothing flagged.
items.y: Surfaced during QA on EP-55347; broken suites hide real regressions in import.
items.o: The failing import tests (email dispatch, team member counts and others) are to be fixed and the suites made to signal failures.

items.s: Changes for Ticketing in registration
items.w: Closed three code-quality gaps in the registration Tickets step - a duplicated constant, an unguarded null-price crash risk, and missing test coverage - with no visible change for participants.
items.y: Found during code review of a related registration ticketing change (EP-56514); addressed proactively as robustness follow-ups before they could cause a production incident.
items.o: A single shared constant for the sold-out status key; a settled nullability contract with a guarded render path and test coverage for the price field; and a new render test pinning TicketingBlock's behaviour (event-over logic, currency/tax, features, page sizing, add/remove handlers).

items.s: Banners sizes streamline
items.w: Streamlines banner sizes (ticket has no further detail).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to standardise banner dimensions.

items.s: Exhibitor event parent/child pair: loaders, error messages and the counterpart index
items.w: Tidies the exhibitor event parent/child approval pair: loaders, error messages and a counterpart index, after the EP-56280 fix.
items.y: Recorded so the remaining risks are scheduled rather than rediscovered; an exhibitor's save could be lost.
items.o: The remaining items around the pair are to be fixed, starting with establishing what happens when the auto-approve branch deletes the row mid-save.

items.s: Scanning a team member with GDPR = 0 does not unlock the exhibitor: member stays hidden on the exhibitor profile and Meet stays unavailable
items.w: Documented that scanning a badge overrides a team member's GDPR opt-out but doesn't unlock their exhibitor's profile or Meet button, and asked for a decision on whether it should.
items.y: Surfaced as an unreconciled interaction between two existing rules (scan-overrides-GDPR, and exhibitor eligibility) rather than a defect against a written requirement; raised to force an explicit decision.
items.o: The ticket documents the gap and both possible resolutions (scan should also unlock the exhibitor, or an explicit statement that scan only ever unlocks the individual); this is a decision/description ticket, with no fix confirmed shipped in the text.

items.s: fix Avatar size="xxs" regression in TagSelect breaking build:types
items.w: Fixes the Avatar size="xxs" regression in TagSelect that breaks the type build and crashes TagSelect items with avatars.
items.y: The regression shipped in 0.5.4 and a red build:types gates nothing.
items.o: The size is to be mapped to xs or restored per Figma, other dropped sizes fixed, and Avatar made to fall back to its default size.

items.s: Make exhibitor manual edits non-destructive
items.w: Organisers can edit published Exhibitor Manual sections and groups without destroying exhibitors' submitted data; only deletion removes data.
items.y: Organisers need to fix and adjust the manual after launch without data loss.
items.o: A rule is specified: non-delete edits keep submission counts, data and status unchanged, and removed fields are retained but hidden.

items.s: move products add/edit route guard onto productInfo and drop the duplicate products request
items.w: Moves the product add/edit permission check onto the productInfo request the form already makes, dropping a duplicate products request.
items.y: Frontend performance, and the limit decision is more correct coming from the backend.
items.o: /api/v1/exhibitor/productInfo is to carry the decision, so entering the form costs exactly one request.

items.s: Deferred registration emails (email_waiting_condition): payment binding, row lifecycle, confirm-race hardening, .ics on release
items.w: Hardens deferred registration emails: binds parked emails to their payment, cleans up rows on cancel, fixes a confirm race and sends .ics on release.
items.y: Edge-case follow-up to EP-56584 raised in PR review, deliberately kept out of the urgent fix.
items.o: A nullable payment_id with filtered release, cancel-time clean-up, race hardening and calendar attachments are scoped.

items.s: Returning registrant keeps platform access before offline payment is approved (account activated at registration)
items.w: Decides whether returning registrants should lose platform access until their offline payment is approved, since accounts are activated at registration.
items.y: Contradicts EP-34905 (no immediate access before approval); the underlying exposure behind EP-56584.
items.o: Product decisions on deferring activation and on payment cancel are needed before implementation.

items.s: New login flow: after "Incorrect login" the email field on the second screen is locked and the way to correct it is not signposted
items.w: Signposts how to correct the email after an "Incorrect login" in the new mobile login flow, where the email field is locked on the second screen.
items.y: Raised as tech debt: behaviour matches the criteria, which chose late validation to prevent account enumeration.
items.o: The second screen is to indicate how to change the email while keeping the anti-enumeration design.

items.s: Point backend front-cache revalidation at /nextapi/revalidate/all
items.w: Backend cache revalidation now hits the frontend's real endpoint directly, removing a redirect hop and a risk of silent stale-cache failures.
items.y: Proactive fix to remove a latent breakage risk (silent stale-cache failure) tied to a planned cleanup of a temporary compatibility redirect.
items.o: Backend now calls /nextapi/revalidate/all directly in one hop instead of via the deprecated /newfront/api/revalidate/all redirect, verified with a single-hop 200 response on both the event and external domains.

items.s: Exclude surcharge/tax from invoice when offline payment method is selected
items.w: Invoices no longer include the credit card surcharge when a delegate chooses invoice payment, controlled by an event setting.
items.y: Requested by ACI Asia-Pacific & Middle East for RACE 2027 (EP-55785).
items.o: With the exclude setting on, invoice-payment orders produce invoices with no surcharge and a net total; card payments are unchanged.

items.s: SessionCardVerticalView does not pass address to MetaInfo
items.w: Makes vertical session cards show the session address, as the other four session card views already do.
items.y: Reported by QA on EP-56654; consumers had only hacky workarounds.
items.o: The vertical view is to pass address through so MetaInfo renders its own address row.

items.s: finish the incomplete Untitled UI v7→v8 upgrade
items.w: Finishes the incomplete Untitled UI v7 to v8 upgrade so the component library matches the design system and upstream features.
items.y: Found while mapping the design system with Code Connect; most gaps are unsynced upstream files.
items.o: Remaining files are to be synced per a per-file audit; hint-text, label, dropdown and 94 new icon subpaths are already done on a branch.

items.s: Switch Pull Integration Service to DI style
items.w: Refactored integration services onto constructor dependency injection so they can actually be unit tested.
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket's brief note that this makes unit testing challenging and should be fixed for full dependency-injection compliance.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title and short description - the specific services and scope of the DI conversion are not detailed in the source.

items.s: Payment analytics
items.w: Adds payment analytics (ticket has no further detail).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to give organisers analytics on registration payments.

items.s: Capture checkout-start events and gateway failure reason codes in the payment lifecycle
items.w: Records a "checkout started" event and gateway failure reason codes in the payment lifecycle, so funnel abandonment and failure causes can be analysed later.
items.y: Raised while the Reg-OT payments refactor (EP-56046) builds the lifecycle model, to avoid a costly retrofit.
items.o: The payment record is to persist checkout-start events and gateway-provided error codes as part of the new lifecycle.

items.s: Exhibitor side repeatable entries and multi-file upload
items.w: Exhibitors can add rows on demand to Exhibitor Manual table sections and upload several files to one File field.
items.y: Raised by FESPA Middle East (about 500 exhibitors, REQ-2026-075); email workarounds defeat structured collection.
items.o: Exhibitors are to add and remove their own rows before submission and attach multiple files per File field, saved with their entries.

items.s: Move sitemap.xml generation to the frontend and make it locale-aware
items.w: Rebuilt sitemap.xml and robots.txt generation on the frontend to fix broken, unindexable URLs and missing French-language pages that a client's SEO agency had reported.
items.y: Direct client-reported SEO issue (Vinexposium), and the frontend already owns the route tree and locale logic needed to generate this correctly, whereas the backend duplicates it and gets it wrong.
items.o: Frontend now generates absolute, redirect-free sitemap URLs per event language with reciprocal hreflang annotations, covering entity pages as well as site-builder pages, plus a corrected robots.txt with a valid User-agent line.

items.s: Restrict meetings for exhibitors without team members (rework)
items.w: Adds a mobile setting that blocks Meet and Message for exhibitors with no team members, with explanatory toasts for attendees and owners.
items.y: Rework of the restriction to one clear rule without changing existing GDPR or connection settings.
items.o: With the setting on, buttons are greyed with a 2-second toaster on all listed surfaces; child exhibitors' members do not count for the parent.

items.s: Global Crawlable Language Switcher & Hreflang Tag Implementation for Multilingual SEO
items.w: Implemented a crawlable language switcher with hreflang tags as part of the Technical SEO improvements effort, per a linked spec not independently verifiable here.
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; grouped under the same Technical SEO improvements epic as the sitemap/hreflang fix (EP-56823).
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

items.s: [OT] Organizer Platform: Add engagement tracking to interactive elements in App Builder Custom Blocks
items.w: Adds click and impression tracking to sponsor banners, story reels and experience cards in HYVE's App Builder custom blocks.
items.y: One-time fix for HYVE to report sponsor performance to exhibitors and sponsors.
items.o: Tracking and a report with date, timestamp, asset and user columns are being built for unique and total engagement.

items.s: Resolve the visitor locale in middleware instead of after hydration
items.w: Resolves a first-time visitor's locale in middleware from Accept-Language, instead of rendering one language and switching after hydration.
items.y: SEO and user experience: pages were served in one language and then navigated away in another.
items.o: Middleware is to detect the locale with a valid locale mapping so the first response is already in the right language.

items.s: Session Calendar View - Toggle On/Off
items.w: The mobile app shows or hides the Session Calendar View according to a backend feature flag.
items.y: Organisers need control over whether the calendar view is offered.
items.o: The app is to read the flag, show the view when enabled, hide it when disabled and fall back safely if the flag is absent.

items.s: Tech debt: relocate src/ unit tests into module Tests/ folders under a separate Codeception root
items.w: Relocated 232 unit tests into co-located module folders under a new independent test root, decoupling the new DDD monolith's tests from legacy tooling.
items.y: Agreed architectural cleanup (design finalized 2026-09-01) to give the src/ monolith its own self-contained test setup as it matures, retiring the @group module-monolith convention and a stale, unused test tree.
items.o: All 232 tests relocated into co-located Tests/Unit folders per module under a new thin src/codeception.yml root with a shared test-kit base class, while universal's own Codeception config and tests remain untouched and green.

items.s: Tech debt: listener priority in ListenerProvider — decouple integration-event listener order from module registration order
items.w: Added an explicit priority mechanism for integration-event listeners so execution order no longer depends on accidental module-registration order.
items.y: Identified as a design fragility in the new DDD monolith that needed decoupling before it caused an accidental ordering bug.
items.o: An optional priority parameter added to listener registration, sorted at dispatch time with a stable sort preserving today's default order, with test coverage for both custom-priority and default ordering.

items.s: Improve waitlist replacement to auto-detect available candidates
items.w: Moved round-table waitlist-replacement eligibility computation from an error-prone backend field into the matchmaking service itself, using data it already receives.
items.y: Improvement identified while implementing Story 3 of the Round Tables RFC; removing the backend's error-prone computation reduces integration risk between Data Science and the Hyve backend.
items.o: The Data Science service now derives eligible candidates itself (applied accounts minus every account already invited to a seat, across all generations and prior replacements) from data /schedule/ already receives; the unassigned_candidates field is removed from the contract entirely.

items.s: Investigate the reason why CH put high load on Dev PG
items.w: Investigated why ClickHouse was overloading the Dev PostgreSQL instance to find and address the root cause.
items.y: Raised on DevOps team feedback as an infrastructure health and stability concern.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title - the description states the problem and references a screenshot, but no resolution or root cause is recorded in the source.

items.s: Required (Important) Custom Category Filters in popup
items.w: Adds required (important) custom category filters to a popup (detail is in a linked Confluence page only).
items.y: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to prompt users to set required custom category filters in a popup.

items.s: [PortalUI] migrate zod to v4 with @hookform/resolvers and react-hook-form upgrade
items.w: Upgraded portal-ui's zod/react-hook-form validation stack to current major versions across 24 files and 88 forms, succeeding a previously abandoned migration attempt.
items.y: Keeps a widely-used dependency (validation spanning auth, payments, registration, and other forms) current and avoids accumulating further drift as the ecosystem moves to v4.
items.o: zod, @hookform/resolvers and react-hook-form upgraded across 24 host files (88 useForm sites), fixing the ~6 new type errors caused by removed v3-only options, with a manual regression pass of every zodResolver form.

items.s: Story 1: API stub — full field list, placeholder values
items.w: Shipped a placeholder API stub covering all ~53 ExpoIntelligence dashboard fields so teams can build against a stable shape before real data is ready.
items.y: Agreed iterative approach (2 Sep sync) to unblock parallel work in parallel with backend data-source development for the ExpoIntelligence exhibitor insights portal.
items.o: A stub API returning the full field set across all 5 dashboard pages, with unpopulated fields explicitly marked -1 and a modular per-card response structure, validated by QA ahead of real data landing.

items.s: Story 2: Page 01 — Celebrate your wins
items.w: Delivered real, precisely-defined metrics (leads, meetings, profile views, peer benchmarking) for the ExpoIntelligence dashboard's "Celebrate your wins" page, replacing placeholder data.
items.y: Second iterative build phase of the agreed ExpoIntelligence rollout, resolving each metric's exact definition with the business stakeholder before implementation.
items.o: Every metric on Page 01 (leads captured, meetings held, profile views, message reply rate, peer benchmarking, best single day, etc.) now returns a real, queryable value with no -1 placeholders remaining, reconciled so totals match across cards.

items.s: Story 3: Page 02 — Your leads
items.w: Delivered real lead-quality scoring, conversion funnel, and follow-up metrics for the ExpoIntelligence "Your leads" dashboard page, dropping metrics the platform can't actually support.
items.y: Continuation of the agreed ExpoIntelligence rollout; scope was actively trimmed (deferring bucketed seniority/company-size to v2, dropping "leads owned by one person" entirely) based on real data-availability findings from the earlier audit.
items.o: Real values now power leads-to-meetings conversion, hot/warm/cold lead scoring, the capture-to-meeting funnel, unactioned-lead detection, peer conversion comparison, and reply-time metrics; unsupported metrics were explicitly removed rather than left as placeholders.

items.s: Story 4: Page 03 — Buyer intent & products
items.w: Delivered real buyer-intent and product-interest metrics for ExpoIntelligence's "Buyer intent & products" page, rebuilding search and demo-request widgets around data the platform actually captures.
items.y: Continuation of the agreed ExpoIntelligence rollout, directly informed by the earlier data-presence audit's findings.
items.o: Real data now powers top filter/category selections (replacing unsupported "search terms"), session-topic interest, uncovered-category gap detection via Product Profiles, and per-product views/saves signals; "demo requests" was removed from the API and UI rather than left as a placeholder.

items.s: Story 5: Page 04 — Your team's engagement
items.w: Puts real data behind the insights portal page "Your team's engagement", covering registration date, logins, dashboard hours, messages and leads per team member.
items.y: Part of delivering the ExpoIntelligence Exhibitor Insights Portal with metrics agreed with Jordan on 2 Sep.
items.o: Each card is wired to defined metrics, such as per-session logins and first-touch lead ownership; the story is in testing.

items.s: Story 6: Page 05 — How you compare
items.w: Puts real data behind the insights portal page "How you compare", showing percentiles against a shared-category peer group.
items.y: Part of the ExpoIntelligence portal, with definitions resolved with Jordan on 2 Sep.
items.o: Paired bars are to show 0–100 percentiles against the shared-category cohort, with the median peer average keeping outliers and a floor of one peer.

items.s: Story 7: Build UI from approved prototype (pages 01–05)
items.w: Builds the insights portal front end for pages 01–05 from the approved prototype, wired to the live API instead of mock values.
items.y: The assembly step that turns ExpoIntelligence data stories into a usable portal.
items.o: The guided journey and one-page report for five sections are to reach visual parity with no mock values; coaching and grow-next-show are out of scope.

items.s: Complete DS part for the service
items.w: Completes the data science part of the AI Event Assistant service (ticket has no further detail).
items.y: Part of the AI Event Assistant (AGENT) epic; not otherwise specified.
items.o: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.

items.s: bootstrap.php: report every unloadable DI class instead of aborting the registration loop
items.w: Makes bootstrap.php report every DI provider class it cannot load, instead of silently skipping it or aborting on the first one.
items.y: Split out of PR #4828 at the reviewer's request; a bare throw was rejected as it changed failure behaviour for about 10 entrypoints.
items.o: The registration loop is to complete and report all unloadable classes together.

items.s: Saved search queries: expose the list endpoint as GET instead of POST
items.w: Exposes the saved search queries list endpoint as GET instead of POST, with the POST route deprecated.
items.y: Follow-up from the EP-55950 review; it could not change there because the verb change breaks the shipped contract.
items.o: A GET route is to be added, the frontend switched, POST deprecated then removed, and OpenAPI and README updated.

items.s: [Spike] Propose the solution for the Logs problem
items.w: Designed a payload-content search feature for the V3 Logs page (covering request/response body, not just metadata) plus a top-nav entry point opening it to clients as well as internal teams.
items.y: Operational need surfaced from real API-issue investigations, plus a business ask to give clients (super admins) direct, self-service transparency into their own API logs.
items.o: A full design was produced for a multi-condition payload search (search-in / field / match / value, up to 5 conditions, 7-day window cap for cost control) running on existing CloudWatch Logs Insights with no storage changes, plus a top-nav entry point to the Logs page for both internal and client users; this ticket delivers the design, not the implementation.

items.s: EditProfileWrapper sends undefined category_id on profile save
items.w: Fixes the standalone Edit Profile page sending an undefined category_id on every profile save.
items.y: Same bug already fixed in MeetingProgramProfileStage; wrong data sent on every save.
items.o: category_id is to be sourced from data.userData, matching the MeetingProgramProfileStage fix.

items.s: Story 31. Removing Accompanying Person Step from Registration Pipeline
items.w: Removed the deprecated Accompanying Persons step from the new Registration Pipeline builder so organizers can't configure an unsupported legacy option.
items.y: Product decision to prevent organizers from configuring a step being deprecated ahead of the new registration engine's broader rollout.
items.o: The Accompanying Persons step is no longer displayed, selectable or configurable in the Admin Panel pipeline builder; existing or cloned templates auto-strip it; participants never see it rendered in the new-engine registration flow.

items.s: [OT Part] Create daily report to be shared with Hyve (DS Part: EP-57186)
items.w: Added click/impression tracking and a near-real-time report on Mobile App homepage elements so client Hyve can report sponsor and exhibitor engagement performance.

items.s: List the source values already arriving that the backend cannot map or display, and decide per value: document, rename, or stop tracking

items.s: ws_time_online_statistics: filter screens arrive as sources in both singular and plural form (_filter / _filters) — decide whether they belong in the contract at all

items.s: Find out why Manager users get superadmin permissions inside a customer admin panel

items.s: Storybook: remove the dead host setup, keep the design system one
items.w: Deleted the host app's broken, unused Storybook setup (196+ dead story files, 15 stale dependencies) since the design system's own Storybook already covers component isolation.
items.y: Evidence-based cost/benefit call: an 8.x migration would require realigning 15 dependencies and fixing 40 type errors for a tool nobody uses, while the design system (expo-react-components) already has a working, actively-used Storybook covering the same components.
items.o: Deleted 196+34 dead story files and the Storybook config, removed 15 unused devDependencies, reduced the host's outstanding TypeScript error count by roughly 40, and migrated the two tests that depended on a Storybook package to the standard testing-library equivalent.

items.s: Add TanStack Query as the client server-state layer and shrink Redux to client state
items.w: Introduces TanStack Query as portal-ui's server-state layer and shrinks Redux to genuine client state.

items.o: A standard query cache is to replace hand-written TTLs, invalidation and loading flags, slice by slice.

items.s: iOS: Sessions and Exhibitor Events hidden only at the type level should still appear in My Schedule

items.o: Type-hidden sessions and exhibitor events now correctly appear in My Schedule and all related surfaces on iOS (matching Android), while item-level visibility restrictions and general Program/search discovery hiding remain unchanged.

items.o: All 23 in-scope library files plus one admin-ui file and one portal-ui alpha-branch regression migrated to chips/Tag, chips/StatusTag and chips/Track, with styling regressions (font size, truncation, border-radius, cursor) compensated for; an ESLint rule now blocks any new legacy import.

items.s: Session Calendar View - Show starting and ending time slots only
items.w: The mobile Session Calendar View grid starts at the first session's time slot and ends at the last, with no empty hours to scroll past.
items.y: Attendees should see the programme immediately on load.
items.o: The visible range is computed per day from the grid sessions, excluding all-day sessions, snapping to slot boundaries.

items.s: Session Calendar View - All Day Sessions with fixed 44px +N button (Mobile)
items.w: Mobile Calendar View moves sessions of 6 hours or more into an ALL DAY banner with a fixed 44px "+N" button, freeing the grid for shorter sessions.
items.y: Mobile adaptation of the web behaviour in EP-57098.
items.o: Sessions of 6+ hours are promoted to a banner in 1- and 3-day modes, excluded from overlap calculation, and still openable.

items.s: manifest.webmanifest is re-fetched on every App Router navigation (max-age=0, no ETag)
items.w: Fixed the web app manifest to cache for an hour like the site's icons, eliminating a needless full network round-trip on every single page navigation.
items.y: Performance and consistency fix found while auditing metadata caching, a companion to the earlier icon-caching fix (EP-55859), removing an avoidable per-navigation server round-trip for every visitor.
items.o: Replaced the Next.js file-convention manifest with a custom route handler serving the same manifest JSON with the same hour-long cache policy as the icons, verified to produce zero repeat network requests within the cache window.

items.s: admin-ui static assets: immutable Cache-Control, 404 instead of SPA fallback under /adminv2/assets, chunk consolidation, CDN-ready base URL
items.w: Fixed admin-ui's static-asset caching, 404 handling and chunk count, and made the asset base URL configurable, unblocking a planned CDN rollout that cuts roughly 40% of server-facing static-file load.
items.y: Direct response to measured server and ALB load from static assets, and a required precondition for a planned DevOps step putting a CDN in front of admin-ui.
items.o: Immutable long-term caching for hashed asset files, real 404s for missing assets instead of the SPA shell, consolidated JS chunks (target 50 or fewer versus 437+), and a configurable asset base URL so DevOps can point builds at a CDN origin.

items.s: Create meeting stats tab in Embeddable Analytics page
items.w: Adds a Meeting Analytics tab to the Embeddable Analytics page, with event, date and meeting-tag filters.
items.y: Extends the Embeddable.com analytics pattern of EP-52392 and EP-54553.
items.o: A new dashboard tab is to show the documented meeting stats, split per selected meeting tag, while the legacy page stays.

items.s: API V2 — Add filter_1 to filter_5 support on sessions/set
items.w: API V2 sessions/set now accepts filter_1 to filter_5, so integrations can set custom session filters, matched in the request language.
items.y: Requested internally and by DLG for session data integrations.
items.o: Filters are applied leniently with per-slot errors, cleared with an empty string, and matched in the request language; done.

items.w: API V2 session read endpoints now return filter_1 to filter_5, so integrators can read back the custom filters they set.
items.y: Complement to EP-57347, requested internally and by DLG.
items.o: Both endpoints return five filter fields in the request language, and delta queries pick up filter-only changes; done.

items.s: Global Search: make the header search term hand-off to category listings deterministic
items.w: Makes the header search term hand-off to category listings reliable, so choosing a category opens its listing already filtered by the term.
items.y: Global Search tech debt: the feature only sometimes worked and lost the term on refresh, share and Back.
items.o: The term is to travel in the URL and be seeded by the listing, preserving existing facets.

items.s: Technical Analysis: Define session image cropping, aspect ratios, and overlay safe zones
items.w: Documents session image cropping, aspect ratios and overlay safe zones across web and mobile, so organisers can design images that UI badges do not obscure.

items.o: Developers are to map image containers, crop rules and overlay positions on web and mobile into a client-ready specification.

items.s: Widen the SearchField page-id helpers to string and make isKnownSearchPage a type guard
items.w: Widens the SearchField page-id helpers to plain strings and makes isKnownSearchPage a type guard, matching the untyped template data they receive.
items.y: TypeScript correctness for Global Search on untyped stored template JSON.
items.o: The helper half shipped in EP-57242 across next14 branches; the story is ready for release.

items.s: Client Manager: authenticated per-event actuals API for Event Calendar and Planhat reconciliation
items.w: Adds an authenticated Client Manager API that returns per-event platform actuals to the Event Calendar service and then Planhat.
items.y: Operations and Data Ops need actuals for the Event Calendar and Planhat reconciliation.
items.o: Unauthenticated or revoked requests are refused and authenticated ones get the specified fields; credential management is an open decision.

items.s: [SEO] Participant Profiles: Implement noindex, follow Robots Directive and Self-Referencing Canonical Tags
items.w: Participant profile pages render noindex, follow and a self-referencing canonical, so attendee profiles stay out of search results.
items.y: Attendee data privacy (GDPR), crawl budget and an SEO audit finding raised for Vinexposium.
items.o: SSR metadata for all participant profile routes is to output the robots directive and correct canonical URL.

items.s: [SEO] Fix 2-Hop Redirect Chains for /newfront/page/* URLs
items.w: Redirects legacy /newfront/page/* and /page/* links straight to the clean URL in one hop instead of two.
items.y: Faster loading, less wasted crawl budget and audit compliance.
items.o: Both legacy patterns are to redirect directly to /{slug} with a single 301/308.

items.s: [SEO] Include Exhibitor, Brand, and Product URLs in XML Sitemaps
items.w: Adds published exhibitor, brand and product URLs to event XML sitemaps so search engines can discover them.
items.y: SEO visibility for participating companies and a technical audit requirement.
items.o: Active, published exhibitors, brands and products are to be listed, with drafts and hidden items excluded.

items.y: Clearer daily schedule navigation for attendees on mobile.
items.o: The multi-day/day switcher is to be removed on mobile and replaced by a dynamic horizontal date selector.

items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: On create with no `password`, one is auto-generated.

items.s: Invalid BM category IDs are non-fatal; valid ones still apply.

items.s: `product/set` matches only on `id`. There is no `external_id`/name fallback, and an `id` that does not resolve is a hard `400`, never a create.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Create requires `event_id`, `exhibitor_id`, `name`, `categories`; an unresolvable `exhibitor_id` is `400`. Products are exhibitor-level — a product cannot exist without an exhibitor.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Product↔event assignment is a `ProductEvents` row driven by `status`: `status=1` or `status` omitted creates the row (assigning the product to `event_id`); `status=0` deletes the row. There is no separate visibility flag.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `update_images=true` deletes every existing product image (and clears `main_image`) before saving the new set, and only applies on update; without it images are appended.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Invalid product category IDs are reported non-fatally in `data.error` and the valid remainder is applied.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `categories/get`: `id` takes priority over all other filters (and `400 Invalid Product Group ID` when unknown); otherwise `event_id` selects the event-scoped view, `timestamp` defaults to `0`. `parent_id=0` marks a root category.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: A hall must exist before a stand: `setStand` create requires `hall_id` + `name`, and the hall must resolve or 400.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: An event must exist before a hall: `setHall` create requires `event_id` + `name`; unknown event → 400.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `id` present and non-zero ⇒ update; omitted or `0` ⇒ create. Applies identically to `setHall` and `setStand`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: On update, only supplied fields change; `event_id`/`hall_id` are ignored once `id` resolves.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Hall names are unique per place (venue), case-insensitively — not per event. Two events sharing a place share the namespace *and* the hall list.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Stand names are unique per hall, case-insensitively. Collision → 400 `Hall can't contain stands with identical names`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Booleans are parsed as the literal lowercase string `"true"`; every other value (`1`, `yes`, `TRUE ` after trim is fine, but `1` is not) sets the flag to false. Sending `is_conference=1` silently disables the flag.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `is_conference` on a stand is the gate for session assignment: only `is_conf` stands are usable as `stand_id`. Flag is stored on `sectors.is_conf`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: The three stand flags (`is_conference`, `is_checkin_zone`, `is_buyer_lounge`) are fully independent; any combination is valid; all default `false`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Halls have only two flags — `is_conference`, `is_checkin_zone`. There is no `is_buyer_lounge` on a hall.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: A hall image may be given as a URL string or a multipart file, on the same `image` field. If both are sent the uploaded file wins (it is applied last) and only the first uploaded file is used.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: An unreachable/invalid URL is a soft error: `data.errors` is populated and the hall is still saved.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: The image is stored under the hall id — but on create the hall is still unsaved, so a new hall's plan is filed under id `null`/`0`. Upload the image in a second, update call.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `getHalls` is scoped by the event's place, not by the event; if the event has no place the result is silently empty (`halls` key absent).
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `getStands` returns `last_update` = `update_timestamp`, falling back to `create_timestamp` when never updated.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `setHall`/`setStand`/`getStands` take a bare `id`/`hall_id` with no event ownership check. Any valid API key can rename, re-flag or read any hall or stand in the client database, including ones belonging to other events.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `exhibitor/set` with `hall`+`stand` auto-creates missing halls and stands by name; `hall` and `stand` must be supplied together, semicolon-separated, positionally paired, equal in count.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Auto-created stands are not conference-eligible (`is_conf` left at DB default `false`) and must be promoted via `setStand`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Undocumented and destructive: `assignStand` is a *replace*, not an add. Every existing stand row for that exhibitor+event that is absent from the submitted list is deleted, and its meetings/schedule/offline-event references are silently remapped to the first sector in the new list. Omitting `hall`/`
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: An auto-created stand gets a degenerate one-point polygon; a `setStand`-created stand gets `coords = '[]'`. Neither is renderable — geometry cannot be set through the v2 API at all.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `location/floorplan` is keyed by `hall_id` and returns `hall_plan{width,height}` plus `sectors[{id,coords}]`. `hall_plan` is omitted entirely when the hall has no `planURL`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Image dimensions are derived by `getimagesize()` on the stored `planURL` on every request — a remote fetch per call when plans live on S3.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `location/floorplan` accepts either an API key or a hard-coded shared Basic credential; it is the only floor-plan route with that dual path. `location/countries` and `location/regions` require a real key.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `event_id` present ⇒ update; absent ⇒ create, and then `title`, `country`, `city`, `start`, `end` are all required.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `clone_event_id` is applied only when an event was produced by `saveObject`, and only alongside the create/update in the same request. Clone runs three steps in fixed order: `copyFromParent` → `cloneTemplate` → `cloneExhibitors`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Clone is fully synchronous and in-request. Nothing about the v2 clone is asynchronous; the async step pipeline (`src/Modules/Cloning`) is a separate admin path, and `Events` keeps a deliberate duplicate of the pre-extraction methods for the API. Expect a long-running, non-transactional request.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Clone copies: the venue/place *including all halls and their sectors* (i.e. the whole floor plan), event files and gallery, product/visitor/exhibitor/session/sponsor/admin categories with old→new id maps stored in `ExpoConfig` block `edition`, permission relations, most config, templates and templat
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Clone does not copy: participants, sessions/agenda content, meetings, news, products' event links, or exhibitor business-area categories. `cloneExhibitors` is called with `$products = false, $categories = false`, so exhibitor→event owner rows are recreated but `ProductEvents` and `ExhibitorBusinessA
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Silent 100-hall ceiling on clone. `Places::getHalls()` defaults to `['limit' => 100]`, so a source venue with more than 100 halls is truncated with no error.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: The error message on a bad `event/delete` id reads `Could not find an event with id = 0` regardless of input — it interpolates `$data['event_id']`, which is never set on this route.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `GET /api/v2/event/setActiveHost?id=N` exists, is live, is undocumented and is absent from the OpenAPI spec. It (a) finds every event whose `host` is the empty string and rewrites it to `host<id>`, (b) sets the target event's `host` to `''` and its `external_domain` to `NULL`, (c) flushes the event
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `notifications/send/{id}` — `{id}` in the path is the event (exhibition) ID, not a notification/campaign ID.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Body is `application/json` (`getJsonRawBody`), not `multipart/form-data`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: "Unlike the rest of the API" is true of the *documented* surface only — `setAccountPushToken` and `updateApp` are also JSON but have no Confluence page.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `user_ids` required, 1–2000 entries; >2000 → 400. Values are int-cast and de-duplicated before counting.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Empty `user_ids` → 400 `No account ids provided`. Undocumented error.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `content` is a language-keyed map; each value ≤235 chars → else 400. Limit is `strlen` (bytes, not characters) — a 235-char UTF-8 message with accents/CJK is rejected.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `subject` must be a string, never an array; `
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: An unknown category name in `subject` → 400 `Category '<name>' not found`. Undocumented error; a typo aborts the whole send rather than degrading.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Category filtering is an intersection: recipients = `user_ids` ∩ category members.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Recipients are additionally filtered to `account_events.active = true` for that event. Undocumented — inactive/detached accounts are silently dropped.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `link` / `linkType` are optional and passed through verbatim into the queue payload — no validation, no enum, no existence check on the target. The `exhibitor`/`session`/`news` list is convention, not enforcement.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Deep-link format is free-form: `link` is language-keyed in the docs' example but typed `any`; nothing normalises it.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Dispatch is asynchronous in SQS batches of 100.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: If every recipient filters out, HTTP is still 200 with `success:false` and no error body. Callers must check `success`, not the status code.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `news/set`: create omits `id`; update passes `id`. `event_id` required and must resolve to a real event.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `status` defaults to `APPROVED`, and `status == APPROVED` forces `published = true`. Because APPROVED is the default, omitting both fields publishes immediately. The OpenAPI annotation's "`published` defaults to False" is wrong.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `title`/`author` are silently truncated to 255 and `short` to 200 — over-long input is accepted, not rejected.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: An unresolvable `exhibitor_id` is non-fatal: a message lands in `data.errors`, the news item still saves with HTTP 200.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `exhibitor_id` must be the internal ID; no external-ID resolution exists on this path.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `tags` is a full replacement — tags absent from the list are deleted.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `product_categories` is a comma-separated list of category IDs; failures are collected as non-fatal errors.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `public_date` defaults to `time()` only on create; on update, omitting it leaves the stored value.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `meetings/export`: `per_page` default 100, max 500 (enforced); `page` default 1; `event_id` required and must exist.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: One row per meeting participant side, not per meeting — the query is over `schedule_contacts` joined to `schedule`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `time_from`/`time_to` bound the appointment, and asymmetrically: `time_from` → `meeting.start >=`, `time_to` → `meeting.end <=`. A meeting straddling `time_to` is excluded.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `last_modified_from`/`last_modified_to` filter `schedule.update_timestamp`, and the emitted `Last Modified` field reads the same column — the "store the highest `Last Modified`" loop is internally consistent.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `update_timestamp` is populated on INSERT as well as UPDATE, so newly created meetings are picked up by `last_modified_from`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: A per-participant status change (confirm/cancel/rate) lives in `schedule_contacts` and cascades to `schedule.update_timestamp`, so status flips are visible to incremental sync.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Every timestamp filter uses a truthy guard, so `…=0` is silently ignored rather than applied. Same for `account_id=0`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `time_from>time_to` and `created_from>created_to` are rejected, but the `last_modified` pair is not range-checked.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: `created_from` / `created_to` exist and filter `meeting.create_timestamp` — present in the OpenAPI spec, absent from every Confluence page.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: Pagination shape is `current`/`next`/`last`; paginate until `next` is null.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: No rate limit is stated anywhere in either data-lake page, and none exists on `meetings/export`, `news/set` or `notifications/send`. The only throttle in the v2 surface is on `statistics/*`.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: No key→event binding exists. The API key is checked against a flat global allowlist; `event_id` is then trusted from the request. Any valid key can read or write any event on the instance.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract

items.s: The v2 router is a bare `:controller/:action` wildcard — every public method of every controller in `backend/api/v2/controllers/` is reachable with any valid key, documented or not.
items.pa: API workflow rules (Source C) — the operational contract
